docs.text: Transport and Protocol Wire layer under gameplay netcode and collaboration: TCP sockets, 4-byte big-endian length prefix + msgpack frames, typed messages, per-frame drain. Gameplay transport ( core/network/transp/ , singleton via get_transport() ) API Signature / meaning host host(host="0.0.0.0", port=7777, max_players=16) -> bool — starts GameServer in a thread, resets role to server, local_id = 0 connect connect(host="127.0.0.1", port=7777, name="Player") -> bool — starts GameClient , sends JOIN {"name"} , waits up to 5 s, returns False on NET_KICK disconnect disconnect() — stops client/server, clears the queue, role back to "none" send send(msg_type, data) — client → server; on server role acts as broadcast send_to send_to(peer_id, msg_type, data) — server → one peer; on client role falls back to send to server broadcast broadcast(msg_type, data) — alias of send (server fans out to all peers) poll poll() -> list[(msg_type, data)] — drain incoming without blocking; call every frame peek / get_peers peek() non-destructive read; get_peers() -> [{id, name}] on server State is_connected , is_server , is_client , local_id (server 0 , client = assigned peer id), peer_count , bytes_sent , bytes_received Caps / callbacks set_max_players(n) lives on GameServer , not on Transport ; set_on_connected / set_on_disconnected live on GameClient , not on Transport Protocol ( core/network/protocol.py , core/config/constants.py ) Framing: make_msg(msg_type, data) packs msgpack {"t": int, "d": dict} with a ">I" length prefix; FRAME_HEADER_SIZE = 4 ; payloads over MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE (4 MiB) raise instead of sending; parse_msg is the inverse. MessageType IntEnum: gameplay range NET_SPAWN = 100 , NET_DESPAWN = 101 , NET_SPAWN_REQUEST = 102 , NET_RPC = 103 , NET_TRANSFORM = 104 , NET_RIGIDBODY = 105 , NET_ANIMATOR = 106 , NET_OWNER_CHANGE = 107 , NET_VARIABLES = 108 , NET_READY = 109 , NET_KICK = 110 , NET_SNAPSHOT = 111 (collaboration types occupy 1–55, 210–212). RPC shapes: plugin events travel as NET_RPC {"rpc": name, "payload": {...}} with the server stamping _sender before dispatch; component calls travel as NET_RPC {"net_id", "method", "args", "rpc_type", "target?"} via rpc.send_server_rpc / send_client_rpc / send_target_rpc . Collaboration transport (separate path, do not confuse) CollabServer ( core/network/serverp/base.py , connection.py ): set_password / set_room / set_max_clients , _auth_ok (room + token check), update_scene_data . CollabClient ( core/network/client.py ): connect(host, port, name, password, room) , set_on_auth_failed . Relay ( core/network/relayp/ ) and UPnP ( core/network/upnpp/ ) helpers serve this path. Gameplay GameServer has none of that: first frame must be JOIN , over-capacity peers get NET_KICK {"reason": "server_full"} and the socket closes. Limits TCP only — asyncio.start_server / asyncio.open_connection with TCP_NODELAY , so high-rate state pays head-of-line blocking; no UDP channel, no encryption, no gameplay-side auth. The server relays only transform/rigidbody/animator/variables/RPC/snapshot to other peers; spawn requests, ownership changes and despawns are consumed by NetworkManager . Transport.send on a server broadcasts — targeted delivery needs send_to ; a client cannot unicast, it always sends to the server. NetworkPlugin.poll() and NetworkManager.on_update() drain the same singleton deque, so run one pump per frame (the manager forwards NET_RPC {"rpc": ...} frames to the plugin). Usage: host() once on the host machine, connect() on joiners, then poll() every frame and dispatch by MessageType . Keep payloads flat and tiny (ids, positions, enums); large transfers go through split_chunks ( CHUNK ) or snapshots, never per-frame whole scenes. Troubleshooting: connect refused → server not started or port blocked/firewalled; kicked at join → server_full ; silent peers → poll() not called each frame or two pumps fighting over one queue; oversize send → ValueError , split the payload. Related: Network Plugin (gameplay wiring), NetworkManager (session component), Collaboration (editor sessions), RPC usage in NetworkManager.send_rpc . Verified against: core/network/transp/transport.py:39-80,82-157 ; core/network/transp/server.py:59-66,108-124,140-160,223-263,269-317 ; core/network/transp/client.py:52-64,91-129,148-186 ; core/network/protocol.py:26-111,147-163 ; core/network/rpc.py:72-105 ; core/config/constants.py:20-21 ; core/network/serverp/base.py:80-87,174-189,233-234 ; core/components/network/netmgr/manager.py:124-172 .

docs.text: Collaboration Protocol Editor co-editing sessions: a host plus guests share cursors, cameras, selections, gizmos, scene edits, scripts and assets. Separate path from gameplay netcode — string peer ids ( peer_<12hex> ), rooms, password auth. Implemented by CollaborationManager ( core/network/collab/manager.py + presence.py / poll.py / watcher.py / scene_sync.py / script_sync.py / asset_sync.py / upnp.py ). Server, client, auth CollabServer(host="0.0.0.0", port=9876, password="", room="", max_clients=32, heartbeat_timeout=20.0) ( serverp/base.py:47-62 , default direct port DEFAULT_DIRECT_PORT = 9876 ). First frame must be JOIN ; over capacity answers NET_KICK {"reason": "server_full"} ; then _auth_ok checks the room (must match when the server sets one) and the password — token = sha256(room + "\x00" + password) or the plain password — replying AUTH_FAIL {"reason": "auth"} on mismatch; clients newer than PROTOCOL_VERSION + 2 get AUTH_FAIL {"reason": "version"} ( serverp/base.py:174-189 , serverp/connection.py:36-96 ). Each peer gets a rotating color; joins fan out as PEER_JOINED , the newcomer receives JOINED {your_id, your_color, peers, scene, version, room} ; leaves fan out as LEAVE . Guards: 400 msgs/s per-peer rate limit, 5 s stale sweeper vs heartbeat_timeout , PING → PONG , TCP_NODELAY everywhere. CollabClient.connect(host, port, name, password="", room="", timeout=8.0) sends _make_join = {name, version, room, token} with TCP_NODELAY + SO_KEEPALIVE ; wait_connected(timeout) resolves id vs auth error ( client.py:77-104,182-189 ). set_password / set_room / set_max_clients reconfigure the server live; update_scene_data(scene) stores the snapshot served to newcomers ( serverp/base.py:80-87,233-234 ). Presence, scenes, scripts, assets PresenceMixin ( collab/presence.py ): send_cursor(x, y, hit?) , send_camera(pos, fwd, up) , send_gizmo_state(mode, hover_axis, dragging) ; oversize payloads auto-split into CHUNK frames ( _send_link / _send_chunked ). Remote state lands on RemotePeer fields: cursor_screen / cursor_hit , camera_pos / _fwd / _up , selected_entity_ids , gizmo_mode / _hover_axis / _dragging , current_tab ( collab/models.py:9-34 ). Default cadences in CollabSettings : cursor 1/30 s, camera 1/15 s, transform 1/20 s, gizmo 1/10 s, ping 3 s, poll 8 ms, scene sync 2 s ( collab/models.py:35-52 ). Scene edits ( scene_sync.py + server _route_message ): send_entity_create/delete/transform/selection/component_update/component_sync/component_add/component_remove/play_mode , each rebroadcast under its *_UPDATE / *_CREATED /… pair with the sender id stamped, plus SCENE_OPEN / SCENE_TAB_SWITCH / SCENE_TAB_CLOSE tab tracking, request_scene_snapshot() → server answers SCENE_SNAPSHOT to the requester only, and _send_full_scene_sync(target) replays entities + transforms to a new peer. Script co-editing ( script_sync.py ): send_script_open/change/cursor(pos, sel_anchor, sel_end)/ops with set_on_remote_script_* callbacks. Assets ( asset_sync.py + watcher.py ): request_asset_list / send_asset_list(target) (paths + sha256 checksums) / send_asset_file / send_asset_request ; _AssetWatcher polls mtimes (interval ≥ 0.5 s) and fires change/delete callbacks. Polling ( poll.py ): _PollThread(callback, interval_ms, stop_event) daemon loops drive _poll_messages , _send_ping and _sweep_peers from the manager. Example session mgr.start_server(host="0.0.0.0", port=9876, password="s3cret", room="LEVEL1") invite = mgr.create_invite(public=True) # "ZARIN1:..." (external IP when UPnP mapped) mgr.join_invite(invite, name="Guest", password="s3cret") # guest side: direct or relay by mode mgr.send_cursor(x, y, hit_pos) # presence, ~30 Hz mgr.send_script_change("scripts/player.py", text) mgr.request_scene_snapshot() # full scene pull mgr.stop() # clears peers, watchers, UPnP mappings Related: Relay and UPnP (rooms/invites/NAT), Message Types (frame format), RemoteCollaborator (in-scene avatars). docs.text: Gameplay Message Types (NET_*) Wire IDs for gameplay netcode: MessageType IntEnum in core/network/protocol.py:80-91 . Values 100–111; collaboration types occupy 1–55 and 210–212. Frame format make_msg(msg_type, data) packs msgpack {"t": int(msg_type), "d": dict} and prepends a ">I" (big-endian uint32) length prefix; parse_msg is the inverse, pack_frame / unpack_frame are aliases. FRAME_HEADER_SIZE = 4 , MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE = 4 MiB — oversize payloads raise ValueError instead of sending. Large transfers go through split_chunks ( CHUNK ) instead of one frame. Server intake vs relay Every client frame first passes GameServer._client_loop : only the allowlisted types are queued locally with a _sender stamp ( server.py:232-247 ). Of those, only transform/rigidbody/animator/variables/RPC/snapshot are fanned out to other peers ( server.py:248-263 ). Spawn requests, ownership changes, despawns and ready flags are consumed by NetworkManager , never relayed. Related handshake types: first frame must be JOIN , answered with JOINED ; disconnects fan out as LEAVE ; PING is answered with PONG inline and never queued. Type table Type Value Purpose (one line) Who sends / relay NET_SPAWN 100 Server announces a new entity {net_id, owner_id, prefab_id, entity} Server broadcast (or send_to for a late joiner via _sync_new_peer ); clients apply via _handle_spawn NET_DESPAWN 101 Remove entity {net_id} Server broadcasts, client sends as a request to server; accepted by server but not relayed NET_SPAWN_REQUEST 102 Client asks server to spawn {prefab_id, entity, requester, pos?, rot?} Client → server only; server-only _handle_spawn_request , never relayed NET_RPC 103 Remote call, two shapes: plugin {"rpc", "payload"} or component {"net_id", "method", "args", "rpc_type", "target?"} Both directions; relayed to other peers; see RPC Reference NET_TRANSFORM 104 Transform state {net_id, t, seq, p?, r?, s?} Authority side broadcasts; relayed ; applied via NetworkTransform.apply_snapshot NET_RIGIDBODY 105 Physics state {net_id, t, seq, v?, w?} Authority side broadcasts (from on_fixed_update ); relayed ; applied via NetworkRigidbody.apply_snapshot NET_ANIMATOR 106 Animator state {net_id, t, seq, clip?, time?, speed?, playing?, params?, trigger?} Authority side broadcasts; relayed ; applied via NetworkAnimator.apply_snapshot NET_OWNER_CHANGE 107 Ownership transfer; client sends {requester} , server rebroadcasts {net_id, owner_id} Client → server → broadcast ; accepted by server but not auto-relayed NET_VARIABLES 108 Synced vars {net_id, vars, t, seq} (legacy data key also read) Authority side broadcasts; relayed ; applied via NetworkVariables.apply_snapshot or generic setattr fallback NET_READY 109 Reserved ready flag Accepted and queued by the server, not relayed, no built-in NetworkManager branch NET_KICK 110 Force-disconnect {reason} , e.g. server_full on over-capacity join Server → one peer, then closes the socket; Transport.connect returns False when it sees one NET_SNAPSHOT 111 Reserved whole-world snapshot channel Accepted and relayed like state channels; no built-in emitter or consumer — user payloads Related: Transport Internals (framing on the wire), RPC Reference (NET_RPC shapes), Snapshots and Interpolation (state channels). docs.text: Relay and UPnP (NAT Traversal) Two ways to connect peers that cannot reach each other directly: a WebSocket relay room, or a UPnP port mapping on the local gateway. Both serve the collaboration path ( CollaborationManager ); gameplay GameServer has neither. Relay ( core/network/relayp/ ) RelayServer(host="0.0.0.0", port=8765, max_rooms=256, max_peers_per_room=32) speaks WebSocket + msgpack ( max_size 8 MiB, ping 20 s): start_sync(timeout) / stop_sync() run it on a daemon thread ( relayp/server.py:19-105 ). Default port constant is DEFAULT_RELAY_PORT = 8765 . The server routes typed payloads with _route_pair (e.g. CURSOR → CURSOR_UPDATE , ENTITY_CREATE → ENTITY_CREATED ) and speaks ops join / welcomed / fail / data {"op","to","t","d"} / peer_joined / peer_left / ping / pong . RelayClient.connect(relay_url, room, name="User", password="", timeout=10.0) normalizes the URL ( ws:// prepended when missing) and the room code, derives token = sha256(room + "\x00" + password) when a password is set, and sends a join hello ( relayp/client.py:78-99,175-212 ). welcomed stores the string peer_id and queues JOINED {your_id, your_color, peers, room, version} ; fail queues AUTH_FAIL and fires on_auth_failed ; remote traffic arrives as data frames queued by type, joins/leaves as PEER_JOINED / LEAVE . send(msg_type, data) wraps into the data envelope (optional target key selects a peer) and refuses payloads over 7 MiB; poll_messages() drains; wait_connected(timeout) blocks until id + auth state resolve. Manager wiring ( collab/manager.py:194-294 ): host_relay(relay_url, room="", ...) generates a 6-char room code when empty and returns it; join_relay(relay_url, room, ...) joins as guest; create_invite(public=True) builds a ZARIN1: invite — relay mode when connected via relay, otherwise a direct invite (public + UPnP-mapped prefers the external IP); join_invite(code, name, password="") parses the invite ( v , mode , host / port or relay , room , locked ) and connects accordingly. Invite helpers: make_invite / parse_invite , build_direct_invite / build_relay_invite , PROTOCOL_VERSION = 2 ( protocol.py:18-23,180-215 ). mgr.host_relay("ws://relay.example.com:8765", room="", password="s3cret", name="Host") code = mgr.create_invite() # "ZARIN1:..." -> share it mgr.join_invite(code, name="Guest", password="s3cret") # other side UPnP ( core/network/upnpp/ , collab/upnp.py ) UpnpMapper(lease=3600) discovers gateways over SSDP and maps ports: map_port(external, internal=None, protocol="TCP", description="ZarinEngine", try_alternatives=True, timeout=10.0) tries external … external+16 , skips in-use mappings (fault 718), and returns {ok, external, internal, protocol, external_ip, error} ; unmap_port(external, protocol) / unmap_all() remove mappings; a background thread renews leases at lease/2 ( upnpp/mapper.py:175-339 ). The collaboration mixin automates this: start_server maps the port when bound to 0.0.0.0 and settings.upnp_enabled (default True , lease 3600); status is a dict with state in idle / discovering / mapped / failed / disabled plus external_ip / external_port / gateway / error ( collab/upnp.py:108-145 ). Extras: refresh_upnp() , map_extra_port(port) , unmap_extra_port(port) ; stopping clears mappings. When to use which Direct connect works on LAN or with a reachable public IP ( connect(host, port, ...) ). Behind NAT without router access, use the relay ( host_relay / join_relay ) — no inbound ports needed, at the cost of routing all traffic through the relay host. When you control the router but lack a static IP, enable UPnP and share create_invite(public=True) so guests get the mapped external endpoint. Related: Collaboration Protocol (sessions), Message Types (invite/auth types), Transport Internals (direct path). docs.text: RPC Reference Remote calls travel as NET_RPC = 103 in two different shapes. Do not mix them: plugin events use {"rpc", "payload"} , component calls use {"net_id", "method", "args", ...} . The server stamps _sender on relayed frames before dispatch. Shape A — plugin events ( NetworkPlugin ) send(msg_type, payload, target_id=-1) wraps the call as {"rpc": name, "payload": {...}} and uses send_to when target_id >= 0 on a server, otherwise broadcast ; broadcast(msg_type, payload) always broadcasts ( plugins/network_plugin.py:94-113 ). plug = engine.plugin_manager.get_plugin("NetworkPlugin") plug.on_message("chat", lambda msg: print(msg.sender_id, msg.payload)) plug.broadcast("chat", {"text": "hello"}) # everyone plug.send("ping1", {"t": 1.0}, target_id=peer_id) # server -> one peer plug.poll() # every frame: dispatches plugin RPCs, re-queues the rest Subscribe with on_message(msg_type, handler) ; handlers receive a NetworkMessage(msg_type, payload, sender_id) . _dispatch_rpc looks up handlers by rpc name and falls back to "*" handlers ( network_plugin.py:115-142 ). handle_transport_messages splits NET_RPC {"rpc": ...} frames off for the plugin and returns the remainder; poll() drains the transport and pushes leftovers back to the front of the queue ( network_plugin.py:144-180 ). Shape B — component calls ( NetworkManager + core/network/rpc.py ) NetworkManager.send_rpc(net_id, method, args=None, target=None) builds {"net_id", "method", "args", "t", "target?"} and routes: send_to when target is set on a server, broadcast when on a server or target is None , otherwise send to the server ( netmgr/transport.py:147-161 ). mgr = NetworkManager.get() mgr.send_rpc(net_id, "take_damage", {"amount": 10}) # server fans out / client asks server mgr.send_rpc(net_id, "heal", {"amount": 5}, target=peer_id) # server -> one peer from core.ecs import Component class Health(Component): @server_rpc def take_damage(self, args): ... Helpers in core/network/rpc.py:72-105 : send_server_rpc (client sends, server broadcasts), send_client_rpc (server broadcasts only), send_target_rpc (server send_to , client plain send ). Decorators server_rpc / client_rpc / target_rpc tag a method with _rpc_type and register it by name. invoke_rpc(entity, method, args, sender) tries the tagged method first ( fn(args) , falling back to fn() ), then handle_rpc(method, args, sender) , then rpc_<method>(**args) . Dispatch order NetworkManager.on_update checks NET_RPC frames first: frames containing "rpc" go to the plugin's _dispatch_rpc , everything else goes to _handle_rpc ( netmgr/manager.py:160-172 ). _handle_rpc drops frames whose target is not the local id, skips client -type RPCs on the server, and invokes the rest on the entity found by net_id ( netmgr/sync.py:323-353 ). Related: Message Types (NET_RPC row), Snapshots and Interpolation ( apply_snapshot dispatch), NetworkManager session component. docs.text: Snapshots and Interpolation (Gameplay) How per-entity state flows: authority sides emit at capped rates, the server relays, receivers buffer timestamped frames and interpolate. NET_SNAPSHOT = 111 is accepted and relayed by the transport but has no built-in emitter or consumer — it is a reserved channel for custom whole-world snapshots; the four component channels below are the working snapshot system. Send rates and gating Each component accumulates dt and sends at most every 1.0 / max(1.0, send_rate) seconds — and only when the value actually changed: Component Default send_rate Inspector range Gate Tick source NetworkTransform 20.0 1–60 pos_threshold 0.001, rot_threshold 0.5°, first send always on_update NetworkRigidbody 20.0 1–60 velocity_threshold 0.01 on vel + angular on_fixed_update NetworkAnimator 10.0 1–30 clip/time/speed/playing/params/trigger diff on_update NetworkVariables 10.0 1–30 dirty flag + sync_on_change immediate send on_update ( network_transform.py:227-234 , network_rigidbody.py:160-168 , network_animator.py:131-165 , network_variables.py:156-168 .) Payloads carry {net_id, t, seq} plus channel keys ( p / r / s , v / w , animator state, vars ). NetworkManager.tick_rate (default 20.0, range 1–60) is an inspector field on the session component; per-component send_rate is what actually paces traffic. Owner-driven vs authoritative Every channel has a SERVER / OWNER authority enum defaulting to SERVER ( TransformAuthority , RigidbodyAuthority , VariableAuthority , animator equivalent). _can_send returns is_server under SERVER and ident.is_owner under OWNER ; apply_snapshot ignores echoes — owner's own frames under OWNER authority, and anything received on the server under SERVER authority — and drops stale seq frames. Ownership itself moves via NET_OWNER_CHANGE : a client sends {requester} , the server applies and broadcast s {net_id, owner_id} ( netmgr/sync.py:355-379 ). Manager dispatch NetworkManager.on_update drains the transport once per frame ( poll() ) and routes by type ( netmgr/manager.py:124-181 ): NET_SPAWN → _handle_spawn , NET_SPAWN_REQUEST → _handle_spawn_request (server only), NET_DESPAWN → _handle_despawn , NET_RPC {"rpc":...} → plugin _dispatch_rpc else _handle_rpc , NET_OWNER_CHANGE → _handle_owner_change , NET_KICK → disconnect() , PEER_JOINED → _sync_new_peer + optional auto-spawn of player_prefab at a random ±2 m offset, LEAVE → despawn that peer's owned entities. State channels resolve the entity by net_id and call comp.apply_snapshot(data) ; NET_VARIABLES without a NetworkVariables component falls back to generic setattr per component_key prop map. Interpolation Receivers append {t, seq, ...} to a bounded deque (transform 32, rigidbody 20) and render at now - interp_delay (transform 0.1 s, rigidbody 0.08 s), lerping between bracketing frames; with interpolate = False the latest frame applies directly. teleport_threshold (default 5.0 m) clears the buffer and snaps on jumps. docs.text: How per-entity state flows: authority sides emit at capped rates, the server relays, receivers buffer timestamped frames and interpolate. NET_SNAPSHOT = 111 is accepted and relayed by the transport but has no built-in emitter or consumer — it is a reserved channel for custom whole-world snapshots; the four component channels below are the working snapshot system.

docs.text: Each component accumulates dt and sends at most every 1.0 / max(1.0, send_rate) seconds — and only when the value actually changed: Component Default send_rate Inspector range Gate Tick source NetworkTransform 20.0 1–60 pos_threshold 0.001, rot_threshold 0.5°, first send always on_update NetworkRigidbody 20.0 1–60 velocity_threshold 0.01 on vel + angular on_fixed_update NetworkAnimator 10.0 1–30 clip/time/speed/playing/params/trigger diff on_update NetworkVariables 10.0 1–30 dirty flag + sync_on_change immediate send on_update ( network_transform.py:227-234 , network_rigidbody.py:160-168 , network_animator.py:131-165 , network_variables.py:156-168 .) Payloads carry {net_id, t, seq} plus channel keys ( p / r / s , v / w , animator state, vars ). NetworkManager.tick_rate (default 20.0, range 1–60) is an inspector field on the session component; per-component send_rate is what actually paces traffic.
docs.title: Send rates and gating

docs.text: Every channel has a SERVER / OWNER authority enum defaulting to SERVER ( TransformAuthority , RigidbodyAuthority , VariableAuthority , animator equivalent). _can_send returns is_server under SERVER and ident.is_owner under OWNER ; apply_snapshot ignores echoes — owner's own frames under OWNER authority, and anything received on the server under SERVER authority — and drops stale seq frames. Ownership itself moves via NET_OWNER_CHANGE : a client sends {requester} , the server applies and broadcast s {net_id, owner_id} ( netmgr/sync.py:355-379 ).
docs.title: Owner-driven vs authoritative

docs.text: NetworkManager.on_update drains the transport once per frame ( poll() ) and routes by type ( netmgr/manager.py:124-181 ): NET_SPAWN → _handle_spawn , NET_SPAWN_REQUEST → _handle_spawn_request (server only), NET_DESPAWN → _handle_despawn , NET_RPC {"rpc":...} → plugin _dispatch_rpc else _handle_rpc , NET_OWNER_CHANGE → _handle_owner_change , NET_KICK → disconnect() , PEER_JOINED → _sync_new_peer + optional auto-spawn of player_prefab at a random ±2 m offset, LEAVE → despawn that peer's owned entities. State channels resolve the entity by net_id and call comp.apply_snapshot(data) ; NET_VARIABLES without a NetworkVariables component falls back to generic setattr per component_key prop map.

docs.text: Transport Internals How GameServer / GameClient move bytes: one TCP connection per peer, each in its own asyncio loop on a daemon thread, frames drained per write. Singleton access via get_transport() . GameServer ( core/network/transp/server.py ) start() spawns the loop thread and waits up to 5 s for the ready flag; set_max_players(n) clamps to >= 1 at any time. The listener is asyncio.start_server with TCP_NODELAY set on both the listen sockets and every accepted socket ( server.py:108-116,126-133 ). _read_frame reads exactly FRAME_HEADER_SIZE bytes, unpacks ">I" , rejects 0 or > MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE , then reads the payload ( server.py:118-124 ). Join handshake, first frame decides everything: First frame must be JOIN , otherwise the socket is closed without a reply ( server.py:140-147 ). At capacity ( len(clients) >= max_players ) the server writes NET_KICK {"reason": "server_full"} , drains, and closes ( server.py:148-160 ). Otherwise it assigns peer_id from _next_id (starts at 1), truncates the name to 32 chars, queues PEER_JOINED {"id", "name"} locally, fans it out to existing peers, and answers the newcomer with JOINED {"your_id", "peers"} ( server.py:161-188 ). On disconnect it queues LEAVE {"id"} locally and fans it out, then closes ( server.py:194-221 ). _client_loop answers PING with PONG {"t"} inline; every other accepted type gets _sender stamped, is appended to the shared incoming deque, and — only for transform/rigidbody/animator/variables/RPC/snapshot — is re-packed and written to all other peers ( server.py:223-267 ). broadcast writes one packed message to every client; send_to(peer_id, ...) writes to a single client; both schedule the drain on the loop via run_coroutine_threadsafe ( server.py:269-317 ). GameClient ( core/network/transp/client.py ) connect(host, port, name) spawns the loop thread (no-op if already connected). _connect uses asyncio.open_connection , sets TCP_NODELAY , marks connected, then sends JOIN {"name"} as its first frame and waits for the reply ( client.py:91-104 ). JOINED stores peer_id and queues the frame; NET_KICK is queued and the session ends; anything else unparseable aborts the connect. _read_loop answers PING with PONG , queues NET_KICK and breaks, and queues everything else ( client.py:148-177 ). send(msg_type, data) packs and schedules _async_send only while connected with a live loop; bytes_sent / bytes_received count framed bytes. set_on_connected / set_on_disconnected are the only callbacks — they live on GameClient , not on Transport . Transport facade ( core/network/transp/transport.py:82-144 ) Method Semantics host(host="0.0.0.0", port=7777, max_players=16) Disconnects first, starts GameServer ; on success role = server, local_id = 0 connect(host="127.0.0.1", port=7777, name="Player") Disconnects first, starts GameClient ; polls up to 5 s for connected , returns False immediately on NET_KICK disconnect() Stops client and server, role back to "none" , clears the incoming queue send(msg_type, data) Client → server; on a server acts as broadcast send_to(peer_id, msg_type, data) Server → one peer; on a client falls back to plain send to the server broadcast(msg_type, data) Alias of send poll() Drain the shared deque under lock, non-blocking — call once per frame peek() / get_peers() Non-destructive read; get_peers() -> [{id, name}] on server only State: is_server / is_client / is_connected , local_id (server 0 , client = assigned id), peer_count , bytes_sent / bytes_received (client side only). TCP only — no UDP, no encryption, no gameplay-side auth; high-rate state pays head-of-line blocking. NetworkPlugin.poll() and NetworkManager.on_update() drain the same deque, so run exactly one pump per frame. Related: Message Types (relay table), Transport and Protocol (overview), NetworkManager. Verified against: core/network/transp/transport.py:39-80,82-157 ; core/network/transp/server.py:29-66,97-124,126-221,223-317 ; core/network/transp/client.py:19-64,77-129,148-194 ; core/network/protocol.py:97-118 ; core/config/constants.py:20-21 .

docs.text: 2D Guide Top-down / side-view planar physics. 2D bodies use Rigidbody2D + one 2D collider and are simulated by the shared solver, then locked to the plane every step. Properties Field Default Notes Rigidbody2D.mass 1.0 add_impulse divides by mass unless kinematic drag 0.0 Inspector 0–1000 angular_drag 0.05 Inspector 0–1000 gravity_scale 1.0 Inspector 0–100 is_kinematic False freeze_rotation False Turn on for top-down characters velocity / angular_velocity Vec2.zero() / 0.0 Setters mark _velocity_dirty ; consume_velocity_dirty() clears it Shape mapping ( shapep/shapes.py:83-91 ): BoxCollider2D → box size [sx, sy, 1.0] , center [ox, oy, 0.0] ; CircleCollider2D → sphere radius scaled_radius , center [ox, oy, 0.0] . Never mix 2D and 3D components on one entity. Plane lock ( scene.py:212-227 , _constrain_2d_bodies ): after step_simulation(dt) every 2D body is clamped — pos.z → 0 , rotation (0, 0, rz) , velocity (vx, vy, 0) , angular velocity (0, 0, az) . Usage in Editor Static ground: BoxCollider2D only. Player: Rigidbody2D + BoxCollider2D with Freeze Rotation on. Pickups: trigger CircleCollider2D reporting via on_collision_enter . Usage in Code scene = Engine.instance().scene player = scene.create_entity("Player2D") from core.components.physics2d.rigidbody2d import Rigidbody2D from core.components.physics2d.box_collider2d import BoxCollider2D from core.maths.math3d import Vec2 rb = Rigidbody2D() rb.mass = 1.0 rb.gravity_scale = 0.0 # top-down: no gravity pull rb.freeze_rotation = True # no spin from hits player.add_component(rb) player.add_component(BoxCollider2D()) ground = scene.create_entity("Ground2D") ground.add_component(BoxCollider2D()) # static: collider only # scripted thrust (e.g. in on_fixed_update): # rb.add_force(Vec2(10.0, 0.0)) # rb.add_impulse(Vec2(0.0, 5.0)) Fixed update notes Same dt = Engine._fixed_dt ( 0.02 default) as 3D; _constrain_2d_bodies runs after the solver step. Same on_collision_enter/stay/exit callbacks and layer / mask filtering as 3D. Related Rigidbody2D, Box/Circle Collider 2D, Collision Callbacks, Collision Layers. docs.text: Box Collider Axis-aligned box shape in local space. The cheapest shape in any solver — crates, walls, floors, triggers, buttons. Properties Field Default Notes layer 0 Collision layer index, 0–15 mask 0xFFFF Collide-with bitmask center (0, 0, 0) Local offset, scaled by Transform scale ( scaled_center ) size (1, 1, 1) Full extents, scaled by Transform scale ( scaled_size ) is_trigger False Reports overlaps, no contact response physic_material "" .zphysmat asset path; wins over inline values when set material_friction 0.6 Inline fallback material_bounciness 0.0 Inline fallback Usage in Editor Set Size / Center , pick Layer + Collision Mask , tick Is Trigger for sensors. Multiple BoxCollider components allowed per entity (compound). Usage in Code entity = scene.create_entity("Crate") from core.components.physics.rigidbody import Rigidbody from core.components.physics.box_collider import BoxCollider from core.maths.math3d import Vec3 rb = Rigidbody() rb.mass = 1.0 entity.add_component(rb) box = BoxCollider() box.size = Vec3(1.0, 1.0, 1.0) box.center = Vec3(0.0, 0.5, 0.0) box.is_trigger = False box.layer = 0 box.mask = 0xFFFF entity.add_component(box) def on_fixed_update(self, dt): rb = self._entity.get_component(Rigidbody) if rb is not None: rb.add_force(Vec3(5.0, 0.0, 0.0)) def on_collision_enter(self, other_id, force=0.0): pass Fixed update notes Shape key ( size , center , friction, restitution, trigger) is re-checked every 60 physics steps ( _shape_check_counter ); changed shapes rebuild the body ( rebuild_entity ). Solver call: create_rigid_body(shape_type="box", shape_params={"size", "center"}) ; bodies with several primitive shapes merge via create_compound_rigid_body . dt is Engine._fixed_dt ( 0.02 default). docs.text: Buoyancy Floating bodies for ponds, rivers and oceans: hulls displace water, waves rock them, currents push them. CPU sampling in on_fixed_update — not a solver body. Properties Field Default Notes density 500.0 Inspector 1–20000 ; object density volume 0.0 Override; 0 = auto from collider (box sx*sy*sz , sphere 4/3πr³ , capsule 4/3πr³ + πr²h ) water_density 1000.0 Inspector 1–2000 linear_drag 8.0 Inspector 0–50 (deserialize fallback 1.5 ) angular_drag 6.0 Inspector 0–50 (deserialize fallback 1.2 ) flow_influence 1.0 Inspector 0–10 use_waves / use_flow True / True Sample height_at / flow_at from WaterVolume sample_resolution 8 Inspector 2–24 grid per axis max_acceleration 8.0 × g clamp on net acceleration enable_debug False Fills gizmo_lines with sample points Read-only submerged_fraction 0–1 displaced/total volume Usage in Editor Add Rigidbody (non-kinematic) + Box / Sphere / CapsuleCollider + Buoyancy , place a WaterVolume in the scene. Tune density vs water_density , linear_drag for hull feel. Usage in Code entity = scene.create_entity("Boat") from core.components.physics.rigidbody import Rigidbody from core.components.physics.box_collider import BoxCollider from core.components.physics.buoyancy import Buoyancy rb = Rigidbody() rb.mass = 500.0 entity.add_component(rb) box = BoxCollider() entity.add_component(box) b = Buoyancy() b.density = 500.0 b.linear_drag = 8.0 b.sample_resolution = 8 entity.add_component(b) def on_fixed_update(self, dt): # Buoyancy.on_fixed_update runs itself: Archimedes + quadratic/viscous # drag + flow-relative velocity, clamped to max_acceleration * 9.81. frac = b.submerged_fraction Requires a collider shape (build fails without one) and at least one WaterVolume entity, else submerged_fraction stays 0 . Fixed update notes Runs in component on_fixed_update(dt) with dt = Engine._fixed_dt ( 0.02 default); force path is rb.add_force / rb.add_torque , applied on the next physics push. Skipped when kinematic or Transform-less. Gravity magnitude used internally: _GRAVITY_MAG = 9.81 . Related Rigidbody, Box/Sphere/Capsule colliders, WaterVolume (environment), Solver & Threading. docs.text: Collision Callbacks Three phases derived from frame-to-frame contact sets: on_collision_enter (new pairs), on_collision_stay (kept pairs), on_collision_exit (lost pairs). Both bodies are notified with the other entity id. Properties Item Value Phases enter / stay / exit , computed as entered = current − prev , exited = prev − current , stayed = current ∩ prev ( events.py:305-307 ) Script signature other_id OR (other_id, force) — arity from inspect.signature at load Component signature Always (other_id, force) force float(ev.get("force", 0.0)) , max over duplicate events for the pair Gating _has_collision_listeners() skips the whole pass when nobody listens Arity rule (scripts) At script load ( hotreload.py:240-248 ): nargs = len(inspect.signature(meth).parameters) # fallback 1 on error self._py_collision_arity[cb] = 2 if nargs >= 2 else 1 Dispatch ( events.py:317-336 ): arity >= 2 → callback(other_id, force) , else callback(other_id) . Components ( _invoke_component_collision , events.py:356-367 ) always get (other_id, force) and ScriptComponent instances are skipped there (they are handled by the script path). Usage in Code # scripts: 1-arg form also works — force is only passed when declared def on_collision_enter(self, other_id): print("hit:", other_id) def on_collision_stay(self, other_id, force=0.0): print("stay:", other_id, force) def on_collision_exit(self, other_id): print("left:", other_id) # plain components must accept both args: class DamageOnHit(Component): def on_collision_enter(self, other_id, force): ... Fixed update notes Events come from solver.get_collision_events() each physics step; prev_frame_contacts is then replaced by the current set ( events.py:348-354 ). Listeners are re-scanned when the entity/component count signature changes ( _listener_signature ). docs.text: Collision Layers Who collides with whom, independent of surface response. Every collider carries layer (default 0 ) and mask (default 0xFFFF ); contact requires both sides to accept each other. Properties Field Default Notes MAX_LAYERS 16 Layers 0–15 layer 0 Per-collider index mask 0xFFFF Per-c Collider bitmask Default names Default, TransparentFX, Ignore Raycast, Water, UI, Player, Enemy, Projectile, Trigger, Ground, Layer10–15 DEFAULT_LAYER_NAMES Default matrix All-vs-all except exclusions build_default_collision_matrix() : layer 2 (Ignore Raycast) collides with nothing; layer 4 (UI) collides only with itself Usage in Editor Set Layer + Collision Mask on each collider. Typical plan: 0 World (everything), 5 Player, 6 Enemy (mute enemy-vs-enemy for crowds), 7 Projectile (world + characters only), 8 Trigger pickups (player only). Usage in Code entity = scene.create_entity("Pickup") from core.components.physics.sphere_collider import SphereCollider s = SphereCollider() s.radius = 1.0 s.is_trigger = True s.layer = 8 s.mask = 1 << 5 # only player layer entity.add_component(s) from core.physics.collision_layers import build_default_collision_matrix, get_layer_mask matrix = build_default_collision_matrix() mask = get_layer_mask([], matrix, 0) def on_collision_enter(self, other_id, force=0.0): pass # triggers report through the same mask test, no contact response Helpers: layer_mask_from_names(names, indices) , layer_names_from_mask(names, mask) . Fixed update notes layer / mask pass into every create_rigid_body / create_compound_rigid_body / soft-body call and are evaluated solver-side per step. per_layer_process mode can additionally isolate layers into on-demand solver processes ( plugin._get_layer_process ). Related Physics Materials, Solver & Threading (per-layer mode), all collider pages, Joints. Verified against core/physics/collision_layers.py core/physics/physics_solver.py ( collision_layer , collision_mask params) plugins/physics_plug/plugin.py (per-layer processes)

docs.text: GS Volume Collider Collision volumes derived from Gaussian-splat captures, so players walk on photogrammetry-style scenes with no mesh geometry. Properties Field Default Notes ply_path "" Splat filter *.ply *.sog *.ssog voxel_size 0.25 Inspector 0.02–4.0 opacity_threshold 0.05 Inspector 0–1 dilation 1 Inspector 0–3 max_boxes 2048 Inspector 64–16384 center (0, 0, 0) Local offset added to every box layer / mask 0 / 0xFFFF Filtering is_trigger False Overlap only physic_material "" .zphysmat path material_friction / material_bounciness 0.6 / 0.0 Fallbacks Usage in Editor Assign Splat Path , tune Voxel Size / Opacity Cutoff / Dilation / Max Boxes . Gizmo draws up to 4000 boxes. Usage in Code entity = scene.create_entity("SplatGround") from core.components.physics.gsvol.collider import GSVolumeCollider gs = GSVolumeCollider() gs.ply_path = "assets/capture.ply" gs.voxel_size = 0.25 gs.max_boxes = 2048 entity.add_component(gs) # static: no Rigidbody def on_collision_enter(self, other_id, force=0.0): pass collider_shapes(transform) expands the volume into a list of box shape dicts (size clamped to ≥1e-4 , center includes center offset and Transform scale); empty volumes contribute zero shapes. Requires the cython occupancy/merge helpers — without them volume_boxes() is empty. Fixed update notes Shapes enter the solver as ordinary box entries through find_shapes_info → compound path; dt is Engine._fixed_dt ( 0.02 default). docs.text: Physics 3D Overview 3D rigid-body simulation in ZarinEngine: entities with a Rigidbody plus one or more colliders are stepped by a pluggable solver ( IPhysicsSolver ), everything else is static scenery. Properties Setting Default Where Solver culverin (Jolt via culverin package) physics_solvers/registry.py DEFAULT_SOLVER , ProjectSettings.json physics.solver Gravity (0.0, -9.81, 0.0) physics.gravity_x/y/z , CulverinSolver._gravity Fixed step 0.02 s engine.fixed_update_dt , physics.fixed_time_step , Engine._fixed_dt Sub-steps 2 physics.num_sub_steps Solver iterations 10 physics.solver_iterations Simulation mode multi_threaded physics.simulation_mode ( single / multi_threaded / per_layer_process ) Usage in Editor Static floor: add BoxCollider only (no Rigidbody ). Dynamic crate: add Rigidbody (mass 1.0 ) + BoxCollider (size 1,1,1 ). Press Play. Kinematic movers: tick is_kinematic and move the Transform; triggers: tick is_trigger and read overlap callbacks. Usage in Code entity = scene.create_entity("Crate") from core.components.physics.rigidbody import Rigidbody from core.components.physics.box_collider import BoxCollider from core.maths.math3d import Vec3 rb = Rigidbody() rb.mass = 1.0 entity.add_component(rb) box = BoxCollider() box.size = Vec3(1.0, 1.0, 1.0) entity.add_component(box) def on_fixed_update(self, dt): rb = self._entity.get_component(Rigidbody) if rb is not None: rb.add_force(Vec3(0.0, 10.0, 0.0)) rb.add_torque(Vec3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0)) def on_collision_enter(self, other_id, force=0.0): pass # (other_entity_id, impact_force), also on_collision_stay/exit Freeze axes: rb.freeze_pos_x/y/z , rb.freeze_rot_x/y/z (serialized as freeze_pos / freeze_rot triples). Fixed update notes Engine.tick_fixed_step ( core/engine/eng/loop.py ) accumulates real time against _fixed_dt ( 0.02 ), caps the backlog at 5 * _fixed_dt , runs at most 5 steps per tick ( MAX_FIXED_STEPS ), then runs scene.fixed_update(fd) (component on_fixed_update : Buoyancy / Motor / CharacterController forces and drives) and finally system-plugin step(fd) . PhysicsScene.step order: register new entities → shape-change check (every 60 steps) → ECS→physics sync → soft-body AABB separation (only when ≥2 soft bodies) → solver.step_simulation(dt) → 2D constrain → physics→ECS sync → soft sync → collision events. Solver-param scoping: num_sub_steps ( 2 ), solver_iterations ( 10 ), erp ( 0.2 ) are project-config defaults consumed by the PyBullet solver (whose standalone defaults are 1 / 50 / 0.4 ); the default Culverin/Jolt solver ignores them and uses the culverin_* world caps instead. Collision callbacks: script methods accept (other_id) or (other_id, force) — arity auto-detected via inspect.signature ( ScriptComponent._py_collision_arity ); engine-component handlers always receive (other_id, force) . Threading: multi_threaded runs the solver in a daemon multiprocessing.Process ( PhysicsProcess ) over SharedPhysicsBuffer / SoftSharedBuffer ; single runs PhysicsScene in-process (required by CharacterController / Motor ); per_layer_process spawns processes on demand per layer. docs.text: Physics Materials Surface response per collider: friction grips, bounciness rebounds. Asset or inline — the asset wins when assigned. Properties Field Default Notes dynamic_friction 0.6 ≥0 static_friction 0.6 ≥0 bounciness 0.0 ≥0 friction_combine average average / minimum / maximum / multiply bounce_combine average Same set File .zphysmat (JSON) PhysicsMaterial.save/load/load_cached Usage in Editor Create a .zphysmat asset, reference it via Physic Material on any collider ( Box / Sphere / Capsule / Mesh / Terrain / GSVolume /2D). Share one ice asset across the rink instead of tuning ten colliders. Usage in Code entity = scene.create_entity("Ice") from core.components.physics.box_collider import BoxCollider from core.assets.physics_material import PhysicsMaterial mat = PhysicsMaterial("Ice") mat.dynamic_friction = 0.05 mat.static_friction = 0.05 mat.bounciness = 0.0 mat.save("assets/ice.zphysmat") box = BoxCollider() box.physic_material = "assets/ice.zphysmat" # asset wins over inline box.material_friction = 0.6 # fallback when asset missing box.material_bounciness = 0.0 entity.add_component(box) Resolution rule (verified): resolve_physics_material loads physic_material via load_cached ; on missing/empty path it falls back to material_friction / material_bounciness with combine average . docs.text: Rigidbody Makes an entity simulated: mass, gravity response, accumulated forces, readable velocities. Without it a collider is static scenery; with it the entity joins the dynamics world. Properties Field Default Notes mass 1.0 Inspector 0.001–100000 ; forced to 0.0 at body creation when is_kinematic drag 0.0 Inspector 0–1000 angular_drag 0.05 Inspector 0–1000 use_gravity True Gravity applies is_kinematic False Transform-driven: pushes dynamics, never pushed freeze_pos_x/y/z False Serialized as freeze_pos triple freeze_rot_x/y/z False Serialized as freeze_rot triple velocity / angular_velocity Vec3.zero() Readable every frame; setter marks body dirty for next sync Usage in Editor Add Rigidbody + one collider ( Box / Sphere / Capsule / Mesh ). Mass 70–90 player-scale, 1–10 crates; keep interacting mass ratios within ~100:1. Tick is_kinematic for movers, freeze rotation axes for non-tipping crates. Usage in Code entity = scene.create_entity("Ball") from core.components.physics.rigidbody import Rigidbody from core.components.physics.sphere_collider import SphereCollider rb = Rigidbody() rb.mass = 2.0 rb.drag = 0.1 rb.freeze_rot_x = True rb.freeze_rot_z = True entity.add_component(rb) col = SphereCollider() col.radius = 0.5 entity.add_component(col) def on_fixed_update(self, dt): rb = self._entity.get_component(Rigidbody) if rb is None or rb.is_kinematic: return rb.add_force(Vec3(0.0, 20.0, 0.0)) # accumulated, cleared after push rb.add_torque(Vec3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0)) rb.add_impulse(Vec3(0.0, 5.0, 0.0)) # instant velocity change impulse/mass def on_collision_enter(self, other_id, force=0.0): pass def on_collision_stay(self, other_id, force=0.0): pass def on_collision_exit(self, other_id, force=0.0): pass add_force(force, world_space=True) / add_torque(torque) accumulate until the next ECS→physics push, then auto-clear — call every fixed step for continuous thrust. add_impulse is ignored for kinematic bodies and non-positive mass. velocity setter flips _velocity_dirty so the value pushes into the solver on the next sync. Collision callbacks: script on_collision_enter/stay/exit accept (other_id) or (other_id, force) (arity auto-detected via inspect.signature ); engine-component handlers always take (other_id, force) . Fixed update notes dt is Engine._fixed_dt ( 0.02 default); render hitches never change physics dt (backlog capped at 5 * _fixed_dt , max 5 steps/tick). Forces apply in _sync_ecs_to_physics , results ( pos / rot / vel / ang_vel ) come back in _sync_physics_to_ecs ; kinematic and Transform-dirty bodies are skipped on read-back (Transform-driven, never overwritten). In multi_threaded mode this crosses the SharedPhysicsBuffer (flags 1 active, 2 dirty, 4 kinematic/teleport, 8 2D). Related Box/Sphere/Capsule/Mesh colliders, CharacterController, Joints, Solver & Threading, Collision Layers. docs.text: Soft Body Deformable mesh simulation for cloth, jelly, squashy props — vertices simulated by the solver, render mesh follows. Properties Field Default Notes layer / mask 0 / 0xFFFF Filtering mass 1.0 Inspector 0.01–10000 stiffness 0.85 Slider 0–1 ; compliance = (1-stiffness) * 0.01 bend_mode distance none / distance / dihedral pressure 0.0 Volume preservation damping 0.1 0–10 iterations 10 1–50 solver iterations gravity_scale ( gravity_factor ) 1.0 0–5 vertex_radius 0.05 0.001–1 max_velocity 500.0 1–5000 pin_mode none none / top / bottom band pin_fraction pin_fraction 0.1 0–0.5 max_vertices 3000 0–30000 ; voxel decimation applies when the mesh exceeds the budget (and max_vertices ≥ 4 ) double_sided True update_com True Drive entity Transform from center of mass recompute_normals True material_friction / material_bounciness 0.2 / 0.0 No asset path on this component Caps 16 bodies, 32768 verts each SoftSharedBuffer Usage in Editor Add MeshFilter (mesh source) + SoftBody . Do not add Rigidbody — SoftBody owns the entity (warning logged, rigid body skipped). Pin top for curtains, bottom for tablecloths. Usage in Code entity = scene.create_entity("Cloth") from core.components.physics.soft_body import SoftBody sb = SoftBody() sb.mass = 1.0 sb.stiffness = 0.85 sb.iterations = 10 sb.pin_mode = sb.pin_mode # none by default entity.add_component(sb) # needs MeshFilter with mesh_path on same entity Solver entry: create_soft_body(entity_id, vertices, indices, position, rotation, mass, compliance, bend_mode, pressure, damping, iterations, gravity_factor, friction, restitution, vertex_radius, max_velocity, max_vertices, pin_mode, pin_fraction, double_sided, update_com, layer, mask) . Teleports rebuild the soft body; COM sync skipped while pinned. Fixed update notes Bodies build in _create_entity_soft from MeshFilter.mesh_path via load_collision_geometry ; results sync in _sync_soft_bodies / _sync_soft_mesh after step_simulation(dt) with dt = Engine._fixed_dt ( 0.02 default). Multi-soft overlap separated by AABB impulse ( _separate_soft_bodies ) for ≥2 soft bodies. Related Rigidbody (do not combine), Mesh Collider, Solver & Threading (soft buffers), Collision Layers. Properties Setting Default Where simulation_mode multi_threaded single / multi_threaded / per_layer_process solver culverin culverin (Jolt) / pybullet (Bullet) / physx (NVIDIA) fixed_time_step 0.02 Step dt num_sub_steps 2 Project config (PyBullet standalone default 1 ; Culverin/Jolt ignores it) solver_iterations 10 Project config (PyBullet standalone default 50 ; Culverin/Jolt ignores it) erp / contact_erp / friction_erp 0.2 / 0.2 / 0.0 Project config (PyBullet standalone erp / contact_erp default 0.4 ; Culverin/Jolt ignores them) culverin_max_bodies / max_pairs / max_contact_constraints 65536 each Jolt world caps culverin_temp_allocator_size 16777216 16 MB culverin_num_threads / max_jobs / max_barriers 0 / 0 / 0 0 = Jolt single-threaded culverin_penetration_slop 0.02 culverin_enable_ccd / enable_sleeping False / True Shared flags 1 active, 2 dirty, 4 kinematic/teleport, 8 2D SharedPhysicsBuffer Limits 65536 entities, 16 soft bodies × 32768 verts shared_buffer.py , soft_shared_buffer.py Usage in Editor Prototype in default multi_threaded . Switch simulation_mode to single when using CharacterController / Motor or debugging solver behavior; per_layer_process for arenas that must never interact. Usage in Code # Gravity at runtime (IPhysicsSolver API): solver.set_gravity((0.0, -9.81, 0.0)) solver.step_simulation(0.02) solver.apply_force(body_id, (0.0, 10.0, 0.0)) solver.apply_torque(body_id, (0.0, 1.0, 0.0)) solver.apply_impulse(body_id, (0.0, 5.0, 0.0)) hit = solver.ray_cast((0.0, 5.0, 0.0), (0.0, -1.0, 0.0), 100.0) Background step order (verified): coalesce pending step commands into one dt → apply teleports/forces from shared memory → step_simulation(dt) → zero 2D out-of-plane velocity → write back with version bump (+ soft buffers) → map body ids to entity ids for collision events. In-process path mirrors it without serialization: register → shape-check (every 60 steps) → ECS→physics → soft separation (only when ≥2 soft bodies) → step → constrain 2D → physics→ECS → soft sync → events. Fixed update notes Engine.tick_fixed_step : accumulate against _fixed_dt ( 0.02 ), cap backlog 5 * _fixed_dt , max 5 steps/tick, then scene.fixed_update(fd) (component on_fixed_update ) and finally system-plugin step(fd) . PhysicsWorker (threaded fallback): daemon threading.Thread , command poll timeout 0.004 s. SceneThreadPool : max_workers = 2 , ThreadPoolExecutor named phys-scene . ECS→physics pushes only on dirty Transform or accumulated force; physics→ECS skips kinematic/dirty bodies; force accumulators clear after every push — call add_force each fixed step. docs.text: PhysX Solver USD/Omni ( ovphysx ) backend. Tensor-driven: poses, velocities, and wrenches flow through bound tables; gravity is baked into the generated scene. Properties Key Default Notes physx_device / device "cpu" opts.get("physx_device", opts.get("device", "cpu")) ; PhysX(device=device) gravity_x/y/z 0.0 / -9.81 / 0.0 Stored; written into USD as physics:gravityDirection + physics:gravityMagnitude ( scenes.py ) debug_draw setter is a no-op ( pass ) Reading works, enabling does nothing on this backend What initialize reads Only physx_device / device and gravity_x/y/z ( solver.py:57-71 ). Honest limitation, verified by grep over the whole physx_solver/ package: num_sub_steps — not read (no match in package). solver_iterations — not read (no match in package). erp — not read (no match in package). set_gravity only stores the tuple and marks _bodies_dirty = True ; it takes effect when the scene is (re)built. step_simulation(dt) accumulates _sim_time += dt , calls ov_physx.step(dt, sim_time) + wait_all() , then pulls transforms from the pose table. Usage in Code from physics_solvers.physx_solver.solverp.solver import PhysXSolver solver = PhysXSolver() ok = solver.initialize({ "physx_device": "cpu", # or "cuda"/"gpu" depending on ovphysx build "gravity_x": 0.0, "gravity_y": -9.81, "gravity_z": 0.0, }) assert ok solver.step_simulation(0.02) Raycast returns the closest body by distance to hit["position"] with body_id / position / normal / distance . get_collision_events adapts get_contact_report() headers/points into body_a / body_b / type / points[position, normal, impulse, separation] . Fixed update notes dt is Engine._fixed_dt ( 0.02 default); stepping runs inside solver.step_simulation(dt) . Pending velocity/wrench writes are flushed before each step ( _flush_pending ). Related Culverin Solver, PyBullet Solver, Solver & Threading, Rigidbody, Collision Layers. Properties Field Code default ( solver.py:16-35 ) Project-config default ( config.py:359-362 ) Notes fixed_time_step 1/60 0.02 Clamped max(0.001, …) ; per-step internal_dt = dt / sub_steps num_sub_steps 1 2 Loop in step_simulation : numSubSteps=1 + N stepSimulation calls solver_iterations 50 10 Forwarded as numSolverIterations erp 0.4 0.2 Forwarded as erp contact_erp 0.4 0.2 Forwarded as defaultContactERP friction_erp 0.0 0.0 Forwarded as frictionERP contact_breaking_threshold 0.02 0.02 Same in both linear_damping / angular_damping 0.04 / 0.04 0.04 / 0.04 Stored defaults enable_sleeping / headless True / True — p.DIRECT when headless else p.GUI Usage in Editor Set physics solver to pybullet . Collision layers work via setCollisionFilterPair : a pair collides only if (groupA & maskB) != 0 and (groupB & maskA) != 0 ( solver.py:281-294 ). docs.text: Music, Plotter and QtQuick Smaller bundled extensions for sound, data and UI hosting — same base class, same hooks, narrower jobs. Verified versions: TrackerMusicPlugin 1.0.0 SYSTEM = False , PlotterPlugin 1.2.0 SYSTEM = False , QtQuickWorldPlugin 1.0.0 SYSTEM = True . Tracker Music ( plugins/tracker_music_plugin/ , rend/ engine: engine.py , engine_seq.py , engine_mix.py , engine_fx.py , defs.py ): ProTracker-style module playback (patterns, samples, BPM-relative tempo) for retro scores and demoscene vibes. Drop a module file, drive play/stop from hooks or scripts, mix under positional AudioSources — music bed plus 3D effects is the intended stack. Tempo math follows classic tracker conventions (ticks per row against BPM). Plotter ( plugins/plotter_plugin/ ): Curve and data plotting panels: profiler traces, animation curves, telemetry — see numbers as pictures during tuning. Feed it from step() hooks or log taps; pair with the profiler panel for frame-time forensics. QtQuick ( plugins/qt_quick_plugin/ ): Hosts QtQuick/QML surfaces inside the editor: animated dashboards, custom tool UIs, web-style panels without fighting the widget toolkit. Use for tooling chrome; gameplay UI stays in the GUI system (GuiCanvas widgets ship in builds, QtQuick does not guarantee that). All three iterate like any user plugin (same lifecycle, same config persistence) and package into .zplugin for sharing. Related: Audio System (music bed pairing), Profiler (plotter data source), GUI Overview (gameplay UI home), .zplugin Packaging.

docs.text: Example Plugin Walkthrough plugins/example_plugin.py (43 lines) is the canonical minimal plugin — every convention in one place. Read it, copy it, rename it. from core.foundation.plugins import PluginBase from core.foundation.logger import Logger class ExamplePlugin(PluginBase): NAME = "ExamplePlugin" VERSION = "1.0.0" DESCRIPTION = "Example user plugin demonstrating the plugin API." SYSTEM = False def __init__(self): super().__init__() self._frame = 0 def initialize(self, engine): super().initialize(engine) self.add_menu_item("ExamplePlugin", "Say Hello", lambda: Logger.info("Hello from ExamplePlugin!"), "Ctrl+Shift+H") self.add_toolbar_button("Hello", lambda: Logger.info("Hello from toolbar!"), tooltip="Say hello") Logger.info(f"[{self.NAME}] Initialized! Counter: {self.get_config('counter', 0)}") def on_scene_loaded(self, scene): Logger.debug(f"[{self.NAME}] Scene loaded: {scene.name}") def on_play_start(self): Logger.debug(f"[{self.NAME}] Play started!") self._frame = 0 def on_play_stop(self): Logger.debug(f"[{self.NAME}] Play stopped after {self._frame} frames.") counter = self.get_config("counter", 0) + 1 self.set_config("counter", counter) Logger.info(f"[{self.NAME}] Run counter saved: {counter}") def shutdown(self): Logger.info(f"[{self.NAME}] Shutdown.") def get_plugin(): return ExamplePlugin() Line-by-line lessons: Metadata block ( NAME/VERSION/DESCRIPTION/SYSTEM ) — copy and rename; SYSTEM = False keeps it in the user tier. super().__init__() then super().initialize(engine) — the second call loads the persisted config; without it get_config always returns defaults. add_menu_item(section, label, callback, shortcut) — menu placement with a hotkey; add_toolbar_button(label, callback, tooltip) — one-click access. Callbacks can be lambdas for one-liners. on_scene_loaded(scene) reads scene.name — scene hooks receive the live object, query it directly. on_play_start resets per-run state ( _frame = 0 ); on_play_stop increments and persists the counter — the canonical config round-trip in four lines. shutdown logs; base shutdown (not overridden here beyond logging) saves config and unpatches. Module-level get_plugin() returns a fresh instance — the manager imports the module and calls exactly this. Any name else and the file is invisible. Exercises: change the shortcut and watch the menu update; add step() counting frames into _frame so the stop message reports real numbers; store a second key ( last_scene ) in on_scene_loaded and print it in initialize . Related: PluginBase Lifecycle (all hooks), User Plugins guide (where to put the file), Plugin Manager (how it loads).

docs.text: MCP Bridge Model-Context-Protocol server ( NAME = "ZarinMCP" , VERSION = "2.1.0" , SYSTEM = False in plugins/zarin_mcp/__init__.py ) exposing engine operations to AI agents: scene queries, object creation, property edits, screenshots, code execution — the same surface this documentation workflow drives. Layout in plugins/zarin_mcp/ : mcp_server.py — protocol server: tool registration, request dispatch, response framing. registry.py — tool catalog: every exposed operation registers with name, schema and handler. handlers/ — one module per domain (scene, objects, viewport, execution), keeping the server file thin. main_thread.py — GUI-thread dispatch: document and view mutations must run on the main thread, so background requests marshal through here. mcp_dock.py — editor panel: server status, connected clients, request log, start/stop. Repo roots: zarin_mcp_config.json and zarin_mcp_launcher.py at the project root configure and launch the bridge outside the editor; plugins/mcp_pack-2.1.1.zplugin ships it as a signed distributable (see Packaging). Workflow: launch the bridge (dock or launcher) → connect an MCP-capable agent with the config → the agent lists tools from the registry → scene edits flow as validated operations with screenshots back. Every mutation is an explicit tool call — auditable in the dock log. Safety posture: the bridge can rewrite scenes and run code — bind it to localhost, gate launches behind the dock switch, and review the request log like a sudo history. Troubleshooting: agent cannot connect → server not started or config path wrong; tool missing → registry for that domain not loaded, check the dock; scene edits lag → main-thread queue saturated, lighten the request rate. Related: .zplugin Packaging (the shippable pack), Plugin Manager (load tier), Gizmos (what agents see).

docs.text: Network Plugin (Plugin Page) System plugin ( network_plugin.py , NAME = "NetworkPlugin" , VERSION = "1.0.0" , SYSTEM = True , DESCRIPTION "Multiplayer transport using GameServer/GameClient over TCP") bridging gameplay code and the transport singleton. Plugin-side facts: Loads in the system tier during editor/engine startup; initialize logs readiness, shutdown disconnects cleanly so no session survives quit. Exposes session state as properties: is_connected , is_server , local_id , peer_count — all exception-guarded, safe to poll from UI code. host(port=7777, max_players=16) binds all interfaces; connect(host, port) joins as "Player" ; both log and return bool. Messaging rides MessageType.NET_RPC frames: send(type, payload, target_id) targets one peer from the server or broadcasts otherwise; broadcast(type, payload) always fans out. on_message(type, handler) subscriptions feed NetworkMessage(msg_type, payload, sender_id) ; "*" wildcard catches unhandled traffic for logging. _dispatch_rpc isolates handler exceptions per handler. poll() drains transport frames, dispatches RPC ones, and requeues the remainder back to the transport — non-RPC protocols coexist untouched. handle_transport_messages(msgs) is the seam other systems hook: returns unhandled frames for upstream processing. For the full messaging patterns, payload shapes and session recipes see the Networking section (Transport and Protocol, NetworkManager, Network Plugin usage page) — this page covers the plugin as an engine citizen: where it loads, what it owns, how it shuts down. Troubleshooting (plugin scope): handlers never fire → poll() not pumped or subscribed after traffic started; double handling → same handler subscribed twice (subscriptions append); session survives editor quit → shutdown path bypassed, always disconnect explicitly in tooling. Related: Networking section (protocol, manager, components), Plugin Manager (system tier), PluginBase Lifecycle (hooks used).

docs.text: Plugins Overview Plugins extend the editor and the engine without touching core files: dock panels, toolbar buttons, menu items, new components, file openers, method patches, extra Inspector fields, native extensions. Two flavors: System plugins ( SYSTEM = True , shipped in plugins/ ): physics, network transport, mesh editor, VR, MCP bridge — the engine relies on them, they load first and cannot be casually removed. User plugins ( SYSTEM = False , live in plugins/user/ ): team tools, importers, level utilities, experiment rigs — load after system plugins, enable/disable freely. Three formats, one manager: .py source plugins with a get_plugin() factory returning the instance. Native .dll / .so shared libraries with a Python entry shim. .zplugin signed packages: manifest + code + native modules + bundled libs, verified against config/trusted_keys , extracted once and cached by sha256 fingerprint. PluginManager ( core/foundation/plugins/manager.py ~203 lines, plus base.py / discovery.py / loader.py / lifecycle.py / ui_registry.py ; re-exported by core/foundation/plugins/__init__.py ) owns discovery, _load_order , activation, dependency checks from manifests, security verification, config persistence per plugin, and teardown in reverse order. Pages: PluginBase Lifecycle, Plugin Manager, Example Plugin walkthrough, User Plugins guide, .zplugin Packaging, System Plugins catalog, Network Plugin, VR Plugin, MCP Bridge, Music/Plotter/QtQuick extensions. Five-minute first plugin: copy plugins/example_plugin.py into plugins/user/my_plugin.py , rename the class and NAME , keep get_plugin() at the bottom, restart the editor — the menu item appears, the toolbar button appears, the run counter persists across sessions.

docs.text: Plugin Manager Discovery, ordering, security and teardown for everything pluggable. One class, PluginManager , three plugin tiers: built-in .py , native binaries, signed .zplugin packages. Discovery and order: System plugins load from plugins/ first, user plugins from plugins/user/ after. Registration order appends to _load_order ; teardown walks it in reverse so dependents release before their dependencies. get_system_plugins() filters the tier; iteration helpers yield instances in load order for frames ( step / pre_step ) and event fan-out (scene, play, window hooks). Replacing a plugin (same NAME , new path) swaps the entry in place instead of duplicating — hot iteration without restarts for pure-Python plugins in some flows. Native binaries: .dll / .so entries load through the native path with _native_plugin_path recorded on the instance; a sibling <name>_resources folder auto-resolves as resource_dir . Bundled dependency directories activate per plugin ( _activate_bundled_libs ) so two plugins can ship conflicting library versions without poisoning each other. .zplugin security chain, verified step by step: verify_zplugin_file checks the manifest (name, version, dependencies list with missing-dependency reports), indexes every entry, and rejects unindexed native modules ( _native/ discipline for .pyd / .so / .dll ). Signatures verify against trusted keys from config/trusted_keys (plus an optional configured dir); without keys configured, verification reports "no trusted keys configured" instead of silently passing. _zplugin_fingerprint (sha256 + size + mtime) gates the extraction cache: unchanged packages reuse the extracted tree, changed ones re-extract. Manifest dependencies resolve (including bundled Cython builds via cython_modules ); missing ones log explicitly and block activation. Configuration: per-plugin security knobs ( check_updates_on_startup , trusted_keys_dir ) feed from the plugin security config; per-plugin data persists through the base-class config load/save. Failure posture: a broken plugin logs and skips — one bad apple never prevents editor startup. Check the console first; the plugin manager panel mirrors load state, order and errors. Related: PluginBase Lifecycle, .zplugin Packaging, User Plugins guide, System Plugins catalog.

docs.text: PluginBase Lifecycle Every plugin subclasses PluginBase ( core/foundation/plugins/base.py , re-exported by core/foundation/plugins/__init__.py ) and is constructed through the module-level get_plugin() factory. Metadata first, behavior second. from core.foundation.plugins import PluginBase from core.foundation.logger import Logger class GreetingPlugin(PluginBase): NAME = "GreetingPlugin" VERSION = "1.0.0" DESCRIPTION = "Greets the user and counts Play sessions." SYSTEM = False def __init__(self): super().__init__() self._frame = 0 def initialize(self, engine): super().initialize(engine) self.add_menu_item("GreetingPlugin", "Say Hello", self.hello, "Ctrl+Shift+H") self.add_toolbar_button("Hello", self.hello, tooltip="Say hello") def hello(self): Logger.info("Hello from GreetingPlugin!") def on_play_start(self): self._frame = 0 def on_play_stop(self): total = self.get_config("runs", 0) + 1 self.set_config("runs", total) def shutdown(self): Logger.info("GreetingPlugin shutdown.") def get_plugin(): return GreetingPlugin() Metadata: NAME (manager key and log tag), VERSION , DESCRIPTION , SYSTEM (load tier). The manager keys everything — logs, config files, load order — off NAME , so renames orphan old configs. Lifecycle hooks, in engine order: Hook Signature When initialize (engine) Once at load; always call super() first (loads persisted config) shutdown () At unload; base implementation saves config and restores all patches step (dt) Every frame (scaled time) pre_step (dt) Every fixed step, before scene update on_viewport_ready (viewport) Editor viewport created on_main_window_ready (main_window) Main window assembled — safe to add docks on_project_opened () Project root known on_scene_loaded / on_scene_unloaded (scene) Scene switch boundaries on_play_start / on_play_stop () Session boundaries — reset per-run state here Capabilities (all verified on the base class): UI: add_menu_item(section, label, callback, shortcut) , add_toolbar_button(label, callback, tooltip) ; dock descriptors in self._docks ; file openers in self._file_openers ; new component types in self._components . Patching without forks: patch_component(name, method_patches, extra_inspector_fields, filter_extensions, wraps) , add_inspector_field(component, field) , extend_file_filter(component, field, filter) , patch_function(module, name, wrapper) — everything tracked by a PatchTracker and reverted by unpatch_all() (automatic in base shutdown ). Config: get_config(key, default) / set_config(key, value) persisted per plugin across restarts; engine access via self.engine ; manager via self._manager ; enabled flag for soft on/off. Native side: _native_plugin_path locates the binary; resource_dir resolves the sibling _resources folder; bundled_library_dir exposes shipped dependencies. Rules: never block initialize (defer heavy work to project/scene hooks); always super().initialize(engine) or config never loads; undo every patch you own even though shutdown covers you; gate per-frame work on self.enabled . Related: Plugin Manager, Example Plugin walkthrough, User Plugins guide.

docs.text: User Plugins Guide Team tools live in plugins/user/ as .py files: importers, level utilities, batch renamers, experiment rigs, custom panels. System tier stays untouched; user tier iterates freely. Scaffold, step by step: Copy plugins/example_plugin.py to plugins/user/my_tool.py . Rename the class and NAME (manager key — unique per plugin), bump VERSION , write a one-line DESCRIPTION , keep SYSTEM = False . Implement initialize(engine) : menu items, toolbar buttons, docks, file openers. Defer project-dependent setup to on_project_opened — initialize runs before the project root is known. Add behavior hooks: step for per-frame tools, on_scene_loaded for scene scanners, on_play_start/stop for session rigs. Persist with get_config / set_config — window layouts, last paths, counters survive restarts with zero file code. Restart the editor (or trigger plugin rescan from the manager panel) and verify: menu entry, button, console lines. Patching etiquette: extend components with add_inspector_field and patch_component instead of editing core files — your fields ride engine updates instead of conflicting with them. Everything unpatches on shutdown automatically. Debugging: console first (import errors name the missing module and line), manager panel second (load state per plugin), Logger.debug breadcrumbs third. A plugin that raises in initialize is skipped with a log — the editor always starts. Distribution inside a team: share the .py file directly for trusted colleagues; ship .zplugin for everyone else (signed, versioned, dependency-checked — see Packaging). Anti-patterns: blocking network calls in initialize (defer to hooks or threads), duplicate NAME s across files (second load swaps the first), absolute paths in configs (store project-relative), per-frame allocations in step (cache in initialize ). Related: Example Plugin walkthrough (conventions), PluginBase Lifecycle (hooks), .zplugin Packaging (distribution), Plugin Manager panel (Editor Manual).

docs.text: VR Plugin Editor and runtime virtual-reality support in plugins/vr_plugin/ ( NAME = "VRPlugin" , VERSION = "1.0.0" , SYSTEM = True in vr_plugin/plug/plugin.py , get_plugin() in vr_plugin/plug/__init__.py ): a runtime core plus an editor dock. plug/plugin.py ( VRPluginBase ) + components/ ( xr_rig.py , xr_locomotion.py , xr_haptics.py , xr_ar.py , xrinter/ ) — session and device management: headset poses feed the scene cameras, controllers appear as tracked input alongside the standard Input API for scripts. vr_dock.py — editor panel: start/stop VR sessions, mirror the headset view into a viewport, device status and per-eye settings. Workflow: open the VR dock, connect the headset, start the session — the game view renders the stereo pair while the desktop viewport keeps the editor camera for staging. Scripts read controller poses through the same Transform/Input conventions as desktop (device-specific bindings surface as buttons and axes). Performance stance: VR doubles the render load (two eyes) — halve render_scale first, then shadow resolution, then PostFX. The profiler's per-stage timings apply per eye; budget 11 ms total, not per eye. Scope note: desktop-first engine with a VR annex, not a VR-native engine — room-scale tracking and guardian flows depend on the OpenVR/OpenXR runtimes installed on the machine. Troubleshooting: headset not found → runtime (SteamVR/monado) not running; black one eye → resolution scale overflow, lower render_scale; drift → tracking loss in the runtime, recenter there. Related: Cameras (stereo pair source), Input API (controller bindings), Profiler, Render Resolution modes.

docs.text: .zplugin Packaging Signed distributable plugin format: one file carrying code, native modules, bundled libraries and a manifest — install by dropping it in, verified before it ever executes. Package anatomy: Manifest: name, version, entry description, dependencies list (other plugins or libraries with versions), optional cython_modules for bundled native builds. Code entries: .py modules loaded through the standard factory convention. Native entries: .pyd / .so / .dll under the _native/ discipline — the verifier rejects unindexed native modules outright. libs/ bundled dependencies activated per plugin, isolated from other plugins' versions. Build tools: tools/build_plugin.py assembles a plain plugin directory; tools/build_zplugin.py compiles native parts (Cython via cythonize when configured), packs the manifest, code, natives and libs into the .zplugin archive. Install and verification flow: Drop the file where the manager scans (or install from the plugin package panel). verify_zplugin_file ( core/foundation/plugins/discovery.py:80 ) validates the manifest, reports missing dependencies by name, and checks the entry index; payload files re-checked by _verify_payload_files (hash mismatch → modified file , unindexed .pyd / .so / .dll outside _native/ rejected). Signatures ( verify_manifest_signature ) verify against config/trusted_keys *.pub files (64-hex ed25519 keys, plus optional trusted_keys_dir ); policy allow_unsigned ( warn default, strict blocks): with no keys configured verification reports no trusted keys configured instead of silently passing. _zplugin_fingerprint ( core/foundation/plugins/ui_registry.py:130 , sha256 + size + mtime) consults the extraction cache — reinstalls of unchanged files cost nothing. Activation resolves dependencies, mounts bundled libs, loads the entry. Updating: bump the manifest version, rebuild, redistribute — the fingerprint changes, the cache re-extracts, dependents re-resolve. Keep NAME stable across versions or configs orphan. The repo ships an example artifact: plugins/mcp_pack-2.1.1.zplugin — inspect it (as an archive) to see a real manifest, native layout and versioning scheme. Troubleshooting: refused unsigned → sign with a trusted key or add the key; missing dependency → install the named package first; stale behavior after rebuild → fingerprint unchanged (mtime granularity), touch or version-bump; native load failure → architecture mismatch (win .pyd / .dll vs linux .so ). Related: Plugin Manager (verification chain), User Plugins guide (what to pack), System Plugins catalog.

docs.text: BSP Map Import (BSPImport) Source-engine map import: parses .bsp geometry and rebuilds it as entities with materials. NAME VERSION SYSTEM BSPImport 2.0.0 False Declared in plugins/user/bsp_import/plugin.py ( BSPImportPlugin , DESCRIPTION = "Import Source Engine BSP maps into the scene (async)" ), re-exported from plugins/user/bsp_import/__init__.py . Parser: plugins/user/bsp_import/parse.py ( BSPFile ). Settings dialog + texture baking: plugins/user/bsp_import/build.py ( ImportSettingsDialog , _generate_texture_png , BSPImportWorker ). Flow on_viewport_ready inserts Tools → Import BSP... → file dialog ( BSP Files (*.bsp) ) → ImportSettingsDialog.get_settings() → _import_sync(path, settings, engine, parent) : BSPFile(path) parses lumps; logs BSP v{version}, {faces} faces, {verts} verts . extract_mesh_groups(settings, progress_cb) → groups {name, vertices, normals, uvs, indices, centroid} ; groups with fewer than 3 indices are skipped. Optional texture baking ( generate_textures , texture_size default 128) → assets/materials/bsp/<tex>.png ; per-group .mat files ( {name, shader_path: "", properties: {albedo_texture, use_albedo_tex: 1}} ) unless one already exists. Scene build: root entity named after the file + one child per group ( Transform at centroid , MeshFilter.mesh_name = f"bsp_{bsp}_{tex}" , MeshRenderer.materials[0]["path"] = <.mat> ), GL upload via mesh.build_gl(ctx, default_prog) when a viewport renderer exists. Settings keys: merge_by_material (default True), generate_textures (True), texture_size (128), center_pivot (False), convert_coords (True), scale (1.0). Limitations (from the parser) Only files with VBSP magic are accepted ( ValueError: Not a valid BSP file otherwise); header stores a 32-bit version and 64 lump entries. Only these lumps are read: vertices (3), texdata (2), texinfo (6), faces (7), edges (12), surfedges (13), texdata string data (43) + table (44). Entities, lightmaps, visibility, physics hulls are not imported. Edge width adapts to file version (32-bit indices when version >= 20 and indices validate, else 16-bit). Textures are procedurally generated placeholder PNGs per material name ( _generate_texture_png ) — original embedded/WAD textures are not extracted. Import is synchronous ( _import_sync ); the async BSPImportWorker path exists in build.py alongside the _on_import_finished assembler. Example # Editor path (no code): Tools -> Import BSP... -> pick de_dust2.bsp # -> keep merge_by_material + generate_textures -> Import. # Result: entity "de_dust2" with one child per material group, # materials under assets/materials/bsp/, hierarchy refreshed. from plugins.user.bsp_import.parse import BSPFile bsp = BSPFile("C:/maps/de_dust2.bsp") print(bsp.version, len(bsp.faces), len(bsp.vertices)) groups = bsp.extract_mesh_groups({"merge_by_material": True}, lambda p, m: None) Verified against plugins/user/bsp_import/__init__.py , plugins/user/bsp_import/plugin.py , plugins/user/bsp_import/parse.py , plugins/user/bsp_import/build.py .

docs.text: MCP Tools Bridge (ZarinMCP) LLM bridge: a Model Context Protocol server inside the editor that exposes scene, components, assets, and viewport capture as tools, resources, templates, and prompts.
