docs.text: Tracker Music (TrackerMusicPlugin) Tracker-module music: MOD/XM/S3M/IT playback rendered to WAV by the plugin's own software synthesis engine in rend/ , plus a pattern editor dock. NAME VERSION SYSTEM TrackerMusicPlugin 1.0.0 False Declared in plugins/tracker_music_plugin/__init__.py (packaging manifest plugins/tracker_music_plugin/manifest.json , entry: tracker_music_plugin/__init__.py ). Registers the TrackerAudioSource component, dock "Tracker Editor" (area bottom , tab Audio ), menu Edit → Open Tracker Editor , toolbar button Tracker , and file openers for .mod .xm .s3m .it . Files (the rend/ engine — not nodmod) plugins/tracker_music_plugin/rend/engine.py — TrackerSoftwareRenderer(_SeqMixin, _FxMixin, _MixMixin) , METER_BLOCK_SEC = 0.1 . plugins/tracker_music_plugin/rend/engine_seq.py — sequencer mixin: sample_rate = 44100 , voices , n_channels , channel_gains , master_gain , set_channel_db(ch, db) , get_meter_data() . plugins/tracker_music_plugin/rend/engine_mix.py — numpy voice mixer ( _mix_one , _render_voice_numpy ). plugins/tracker_music_plugin/rend/engine_fx.py — instrument/sample helpers ( _sample_for_instrument , _sample_volume , _sample_wave , _sample_loop ). plugins/tracker_music_plugin/rend/defs.py — constants _NTSC_SR = 8287.0 , _AMIGA_CLOCK = 3546894.6 , _RENDER_VERSION = 3 , _MOD_PERIODS , _NOTE_NAMES , plus _note_to_midi() and _parse_effect() . plugins/tracker_music_plugin/rend/service.py — TrackerRenderService(cache_dir, sample_rate=44100) , load_module(path) , render_to_wav_file(pcm, path, sample_rate) , find_external_renderer() . plugins/tracker_music_plugin/rend/voice.py — _Voice . plugins/tracker_music_plugin/tracker_audio_source.py — TrackerAudioSource(AudioSource) component + patch_audio_source_play() . Optional Cython mixer: fastmix.pyx / fastmix.c , loaded via import_extension ( core/foundation/plugin_cython.py ), built by ensure_extensions . Note: module parsing is delegated to the vendored plugins/tracker_music_plugin/libs/nodmod ( load_song ); all synthesis is the rend/ engine above. API TrackerRenderService.render_wav(module_path, quality="software") → cached .wav path (key includes file hash, sample rate, _RENDER_VERSION ) or None . quality="external" tries openmpt123 / ffmpeg first, then falls back to the software renderer ( TrackerSoftwareRenderer(sample_rate).render(song) → stereo 16-bit WAV). TrackerAudioSource fields: clip_path (module file), render_quality ( "software" / "external" ), readonly song_length_sec , channels_count (filled from song.get_song_info() ). Supported extensions ( TRACKER_EXTS ): .mod .xm .s3m .it .669 .mtm .stm .ult . play() renders the module to WAV and plays it through AudioSource , restoring the original clip_path afterwards. The plugin also patches stock AudioSource.play ( ComponentPatcher.wrap_method , before/after) so a plain AudioSource with a tracker clip_path renders automatically too. Playing a track — example class Jukebox: module: str = "assets/music/level1.xm" def on_start(self): src = self._entity.get_component_by_name("TrackerAudioSource") if src is None: return src.clip_path = self.module src.render_quality = "software" # or "external" for openmpt123/ffmpeg src.play() Logger.info(f"Playing: {src.channels_count} ch, {src.song_length_sec:.1f} s") Steps: add TrackerAudioSource to an entity → set Module to the .xm / .mod file → press Play (or call play() ). Open Edit → Open Tracker Editor (or double-click a module file) to inspect patterns via song.get_song_info() . docs.text: Physics Tooling Plugins Four plugins around the physics core: simulation, debug visualisation, editor drag, and mesh editing. NAME VERSION SYSTEM PhysicsPlugin 0.4.0 True PhysicsVisualisation 1.1.0 True PhysicsDragPlugin 0.1.0 False MeshEditorPlugin 1.0.0 False Declared in plugins/physics_plug/plugin.py , plugins/physviz/plugin.py , plugins/physics_drag_plugin.py , plugins/mesh_editor_plugin.py . What each does PhysicsPlugin ( 0.4.0 , SYSTEM) — the simulation itself ( DESCRIPTION = "Physics system with shared-memory parallel simulation." ). simulation_mode from project config: multi_threaded (default, PhysicsProcess shared-memory worker), single (in-process solver), per_layer_process . Solver resolved via physics_solvers.registry ( normalize , get_module_class , is_available , fallback to DEFAULT_SOLVER ). Key API: physics_scene property, ensure_single_mode() -> bool , hooks on_scene_loaded / on_scene_unloaded / on_project_opened . Note: CharacterController only works in-process — without it the controller logs Use single-threaded physics mode (simulation_mode='single') for characters. PhysicsVisualisation ( 1.1.0 , SYSTEM) — debug arrows through the Gizmos system (tag from physviz/draw.py ): velocity / acceleration / moment vectors, contacts, joints, colliders. Settings (all live-patchable via configure(patch) ): enabled , show_velocity/acceleration/moment/contacts/joints/colliders , only_selected , show_labels , show_editor/show_runtime , velocity_scale (0.3), acceleration_scale (0.05), moment_scale (0.05), max_length (2.5), min_magnitude (0.1), smooth (0.35), accel_spike (200.0), moment_spike (400.0), label_cap (48), contact_normal_length (0.6). Panel: dock "Physics Visualisation" (area right ), menu Tools → Physics Visualisation , 50 ms QTimer refresh in editor, step(dt) redraw in play. PhysicsDragPlugin ( 0.1.0 , editor tool) — Ctrl+Shift+LeftClick drags simulated bodies in play mode . Installs an event filter on the viewport ( on_viewport_ready ); on press it casts physics_scene.ray_cast(origin, direction, 1000.0) and accepts only entities with a non-kinematic Rigidbody with mass > 0 ; move updates update_drag_constraint(id, target) (plane-projected via viewport.screen_to_plane ), release calls remove_drag_constraint(id) . Scene handle is refreshed from PhysicsPlugin.physics_scene on initialize / on_scene_loaded / on_play_start . MeshEditorPlugin ( 1.0.0 , ProBuilder-style) — one menu item Mesh Editor → Open Mesh Editor (shortcut Ctrl+Shift+M ) opening the main window's _mesh_editor for the first selected entity. Dragging a body — example # 1. Press Play (drag works only when engine.play_mode is True). # 2. Hold Ctrl+Shift, left-click a dynamic Rigidbody in the viewport. # 3. Move the mouse: the hit body follows on the grab plane # (debug line body -> anchor while dragging). # 4. Release the mouse button: constraint removed, body keeps velocity. # # Script-side equivalent of what the filter does: ps = engine.plugin_manager.get("PhysicsPlugin").physics_scene origin, direction = viewport.screen_to_ray(x, y) hit = ps.ray_cast(origin, direction, 1000.0) # {"entity_id", "body_id", "position"} cid = ps.create_drag_constraint(hit["body_id"], Vec3(*hit["position"])) ps.update_drag_constraint(cid, new_target) ps.remove_drag_constraint(cid) Verified against plugins/physics_plug/plugin.py , plugins/physviz/plugin.py , plugins/physics_drag_plugin.py , plugins/mesh_editor_plugin.py , core/components/physics/character/jump_slope.py (single-mode warning).

QtQuickWorldPlugin is declared as QtQuickWorldPluginBase in plugins/qt_quick_plugin/plug/plugin.py (manifest plugins/qt_quick_plugin/manifest.json , provides: {} ). Files plugins/plotter_plugin/panel.py — PlotterPanel(engine, plugin, persist=True) : pickers + ChartWidget , set_active(bool) . plugins/plotter_plugin/plotter/ — ChartWidget , chart/series.py ( Series.plot(...) ), canvas backends, sidebar, palette. plugins/qt_quick_plugin/plug/plugin.py — runtime attach, render hook, QtQuick → Create … menu (Button, Label, Slider, Field, Check, Bar, Switch, Dial, Combo, Spin, Panel, Image), Refresh All , Diagnose , QuickUI toolbar button. plugins/qt_quick_plugin/components/quick_view.py — QuickView base component. plugins/qt_quick_plugin/components/controls/ — QuickButton , QuickLabel , QuickSlider , … ( QUICK_ALL_TYPES ). plugins/qt_quick_plugin/runtime/ , gl/ , interact/ — QML runtime, GL renderer, picking. API Plotter: dock "Plotter" (area left , icon fa5s.chart-line ), menu Tools → Open Plotter / Tools → New Plotter Window , toolbar New Plotter . PlotterPanel polls on a QTimer ( refresh_interval default 100 ms, history_limit default 2000 from plugin config): pick X (time or entity property) and Y (entity property via EntityPropertyPicker ), press Track , watch ChartWidget(show_legend, show_toolbar) ; Clear drops all series. QuickView fields: qml_text / qml_file ( *.qml ), width_px / height_px (32–2048, default 512), size_x / size_y meters (default 1.0), transparent (default True), billboard ( Off / Full / Y ), interactive (default True), opacity , render_order , double_sided , animated , tint . QuickButton adds text (default "Button" ), font_size (default 28), checkable / checked , readonly click_count , plus add_on_clicked(fn) / remove_on_clicked(fn) / click() / get_value() . Example — chart plus world-space button # Plotter (editor): select any entity, open the Plotter dock, # Y-picker -> Transform -> position.x, press "Track", press Play. # The chart samples the property every refresh_interval ms. # QtQuick world button (script side, on an entity with QuickButton): def on_start(self): btn = self._entity.get_component_by_name("QuickButton") btn.text = "Launch" btn.add_on_clicked(self._on_launch) def _on_launch(self, btn): Logger.info(f"Launched, clicks={btn.click_count}") Menu path instead of code: QtQuick → Create Button spawns a QuickButton entity; edit Text / Size X m / Billboard in the Inspector. docs.text: VR Session Setup (VRPlugin) Stereo VR integration: OpenXR session, XR rig entities, and the editor control dock. NAME VERSION SYSTEM VRPlugin 1.0.0 True Declared in plugins/vr_plugin/plug/plugin.py ( VRPluginBase , DESCRIPTION = "VR display integration with OpenXR" ). Factory get_plugin() lives in plugins/vr_plugin/plug/__init__.py . Files plugins/vr_plugin/plug/plugin.py — VRPluginBase : dock registration ( "VR Control" , area bottom ), toggle_vr() , spawn_xr_rig(engine) , ensure_vr_entities() / remove_vr_entities() , hooks on_scene_loaded / on_viewport_ready . plugins/vr_plugin/components/xr_rig.py — XRRig , XRTrackedPoseDriver , XRController , XRHand , XRCull . plugins/vr_plugin/components/xr_locomotion.py — XRSmoothMoveProvider , XRSnapTurnProvider , XRTeleportationProvider . plugins/vr_plugin/components/xr_haptics.py — XRHaptics . plugins/vr_plugin/components/xr_ar.py — ARSession , ARCameraBackground , ARPlaneManager , ARRaycastManager , ARAnchorManager , ARPointCloudManager . plugins/vr_plugin/components/xrinter/ — XRInteractionManager , XRRayInteractor , XRDirectInteractor , XRPokeInteractor , XRGrabInteractable . plugins/vr_plugin/vr_dock.py — VRControlWidget editor panel. plugins/vr_plugin/core/ — runtime: session.py / session2.py (OpenXR session), state.py / state2.py (state, is_available() ), swapchain.py (eye framebuffers), controllers.py (controller state, haptics). API XRRig defaults ( xr_rig.py ): move_speed = 5.0 , turn_speed = 80.0 , vert_speed = 2.5 , acceleration = 12.0 , damping = 8.0 , ipd = 0.063 , tracking_origin_mode = "Floor" , enable_locomotion = True . XRTrackedPoseDriver.pose_source is one of Head, CenterEye, LeftEye, RightEye, LeftHand, RightHand (default Head ). XRController(controller_hand) is "Left" / "Right" with SendHapticImpulse(amplitude, duration, frequency) / CancelHaptic() . Core functions ( core/__init__.py , state.py ): is_available() , is_active() , session_running() , get_ipd() / set_ipd() / reset_ipd() , reset_hmd_origin() , is_eye_view() / set_eye_view() / toggle_eye_view() , get_controllers() , get_hmd_pos_offset() . Eye defaults: textures 1440x1600 , vertical FOV 90 deg, horizontal FOV 100 deg. Requirements Yes — an OpenXR runtime is required. is_available() returns _XR_AVAILABLE , which is True only when import xr succeeds ( core/state.py ). The dock's Initialize VR button stays disabled ( setEnabled(avail) ) until then, and session.initialize(ctx) refuses to start without it. Without a working OpenXR runtime on the machine, VR stays Off and the scene runs on the desktop camera. Session setup example # 1. Open the "VR Control" dock (bottom area) and press "Initialize VR". # Status flips Off -> Initializing... -> Active (333 ms refresh timer). # 2. Spawn the rig from code (same call the dock's "Spawn XR Rig" button makes): rig = plugin.spawn_xr_rig(engine) # Creates: XRRig (+ XRRig, XRInteractionManager, move/snap/teleport providers) # + XRHMD (tracked pose driver, eye height 1.6 m) # + XRControllerLeft / XRControllerRight (pose driver + XRController + XRHand) # 3. Tune in the dock: IPD slider 10..200 mm (default 63 -> 0.063 m), # "Reset HMD Origin", "View: Eye/Desktop" toggle. from plugins.vr_plugin import core as vr_core vr_core.set_ipd(0.063) vr_core.set_eye_view(True) # Eye stereo vs Desktop mirror When the session is active, on_scene_loaded auto-spawns the rig; when VR is off, rig entities are removed from the scene. Verified against plugins/vr_plugin/plug/plugin.py , plugins/vr_plugin/plug/__init__.py , plugins/vr_plugin/vr_dock.py , plugins/vr_plugin/components/xr_rig.py , plugins/vr_plugin/components/xr_locomotion.py , plugins/vr_plugin/components/xr_haptics.py , plugins/vr_plugin/components/xr_ar.py , plugins/vr_plugin/core/__init__.py , plugins/vr_plugin/core/state.py , plugins/vr_plugin/core/session.py .

docs.text: Glossary and FAQ Glossary Entity — scene object with UUID, name, parent/children, tags, layer, active toggle. Behavior comes only from components. Component — data + lifecycle hooks ( on_awake/on_start/on_update/on_fixed_update/on_destroy/on_enable/on_disable ) auto-discovered via ComponentRegistry . ScriptComponent — the component that hosts a user .py behavior: script_path + script_fields + hot_reload . Behavior class — first class in the script file declaring a lifecycle/collision/gizmo member or _inspector_buttons ; no base class, constructed with no arguments. Inspector field — annotated class attribute rendered as a widget; values persist per instance in the scene. Play — run mode: scripts load, on_awake / on_start fire, per-frame updates run. Gizmo methods also run outside Play. Hot-reload — mtime-triggered instance recreation during Play preserving Inspector values. Fixed update — physics-clock callback with stable dt ( 0.02 default); render dt is already time-scaled. Prefab ( .zpep ) — saved entity subtree with stable GUIDs; instances remap GUIDs and keep overrides. Cython companion — sibling .pyx auto-built into cache/cython on first import, rebuilt when newer. Time scale — multiplier applied to render dt ; fixed-step dt stays constant. FAQ Script does nothing on Play? The Script field is empty or points at a moved file ( script_path is project-root-relative). Re-pick it; the Check action reports file:line errors. Vec3.rotate missing? Correct — rotation lives on Transform.rotate(Vec3 degrees) . Vec3 offers dot/cross/length/normalized/lerp , not rotate . core.math3d import fails? Import from core.maths.math3d . The Check button suggests exactly this. Edit during Play lost state? Expected: __init__ state resets on reload by design; keep tunable state in Inspector fields and rebuild caches in on_awake / on_start . Ball falls through the floor? Missing collider, Is Trigger without contact handling, or Is Kinematic where solver motion is expected. No sound? clip_path empty/unresolvable, AudioListener missing from the camera entity, or play() called with no AudioSystem in a headless context. First Play is slow with .pyx ? One-time native compile into cache/cython ; later runs reuse it. The Check button validates .pyx without a C compiler.

Full text in LICENSE at the repository root. Requirements (from README.md ) Python 3.13+, PySide6 ≥ 6.6.0, ModernGL ≥ 5.10.0, NumPy ≥ 1.26.0, system OpenAL for audio, bundled Assimp DLL/SO for mesh import. Full list in requirements.txt . OpenGL 4.6 Core Profile. All engine math is numpy.float64 ; float32 conversion happens only at GPU upload. Entry points and tests python main.py — editor. python player.py Scene.zpes — run a scene (default "SampleScene.zpes" ). python build_nuitka.py — Nuitka standalone build (settings in BuildSettings.json ). python setup.py — compiles the 34 engine Cython extensions from core/pyx/*.pyx : _convex_hull , _bvh_build , _raytracing_data , math_helpers , _math_vec , _culling , _transform_batch , _render_utils , _physics_utils , _core_batch , _types , _ecs_batch , _render_batch , _octree_batch , _constraint_batch , _curve_batch , _constraint_update , _physics_sync , _mesh_import , _skinning , _ik , _physbone , _audio_dsp , _raycast , _shadow_batch , _scene_query , _render_collect , _math_mat4 , _vr_batch , _nav_batch , _splat_sort , _gs_volume , _sky_astro (plus _shader_parse sources). Windows default toolchain is the auto-downloaded compact MinGW-w64. Smoke tests in tests/smoke/ : test_scripting , test_script_inspector , test_script_cython , test_engine_embed , test_relpaths , test_import_materials , test_mesh_import_persist , test_ik_numeric , test_blendshapes , test_compression_async , test_digest_dedup , test_duplicate_skinned , test_embed2 , test_embed_outside , test_prop_picker , test_soft_remote , plus tests/libs/test_library_packs.py . Changelog and roadmap No CHANGELOG.md ships with the repository: the git history is the change record. The scripting contract source of truth is docs/scripting.md in the engine repo. Verifiable direction from the code (not promises): gameplay-side networking is stubs ( host / connect / send / broadcast / poll awaiting a transport; NetworkIdentity is a stub component), while ECS, editor, rendering, physics, audio, GUI, prefabs, scripting hot-reload and user Cython companions are implemented and covered by the smoke tests above.

docs.text: Area Light Panel light: AreaLight ( core/components/lighting/lightp/shadows.py:79-185 ) with nit brightness, rect/disk shape and multi-sample shadows. Home · Section index Overview Surface brightness in nits (cd/m²): monitor 200 , office panel 500 , overcast sky 2000 , softbox 10000 . Same nits on a bigger panel lights more ( shadows.py:92 ). Gizmo draws the rect frame, optional disk ring and double-sided back frame ( shadows.py:118-161 ). Properties name type default description color color3 [1.0, 1.0, 1.0] Light color ( shadows.py:91 ). intensity float nits (0–200000) 100.0 Surface brightness ( shadows.py:92,106 ). range float (0–10000) 10.0 Cutoff distance ( shadows.py:93,107 ). area_type LightAreaType RECT rect / disk ( shadows.py:95,108 ). area_width float (0.01–100) 1.0 Panel width, m ( shadows.py:96,109 ). area_height float (0.01–100) 1.0 Panel height, m ( shadows.py:97,110 ). area_double_sided bool False Emit from both faces ( shadows.py:98,111 ). area_samples int (1–64) 6 Shadow samples ( shadows.py:99,112 ). area_shadow_bias float (0–0.1) 0.005 Shadow bias ( shadows.py:100,113 ). cast_shadows bool True Needs active AreaShadow ( shadows.py:102,114 ). ## Usage in Editor Scale via Area Width/Height, not the transform. Use Disk for round softboxes; enable Double Sided for paper lanterns. Raise Samples to soften, Bias to fix acne. ## Usage in Code al.area_type = LightAreaType.DISK al.area_width = 2.0 al.area_samples = 12 Related pages Light , Shadows Verified against core/components/lighting/lightp/shadows.py:79-185 core/components/lighting/lightp/light.py:20-22 ( LightAreaType )

Home · Section index Overview Computes a transmittance/multi-scatter LUT ( atmosp/compute.py , AtmosphereLutMixin ); _resolution_scale scales the LUT. docs.text: Camera Scene camera: Camera component ( core/components/rendering/cameras/camera.py ) with perspective/orthographic projection, depth ordering and native/custom render size. Home · Section index Overview View matrix is Mat4.look_at(position, position + forward, up) ; projection is Mat4.perspective(fov, aspect, near, far) or orthographic with half_w = ortho_size * aspect ( camera.py:56-69 ). Gizmo draws the frustum from near/far corners ( camera.py:100-143 ). Base clamps and render-size logic live in CameraBase ( camera_base.py ). Properties name type default description fov float (1.0–179.0) 60.0 Perspective field of view ( camera.py:36 , camera_base.py:19 ). near float (≥0.001) 0.01 Near clip ( camera.py:37 , camera_base.py:20 ). far float (≥0.1) 1000.0 Far clip ( camera.py:38 , camera_base.py:21 ). projection CameraProjection PERSPECTIVE perspective / orthographic ( camera.py:39,52 ). ortho_size float (≥0.001) 5.0 Orthographic half-extent ( camera.py:40 , camera_base.py:23 ). depth int (−100…100) 0 Draw-order priority ( camera.py:42,54 ). render_scale float (0.1–1.0) 1.0 Resolution multiplier ( camera.py:43 , camera_base.py:24 ). resolution_mode CameraResolutionMode native native follows viewport, custom uses w/h ( camera.py:44 ). resolution_w int (1–16384) 1920 Custom width ( camera.py:45 ). resolution_h int (1–16384) 1080 Custom height ( camera.py:46 ). clear_color color4 (code only) [0.15, 0.15, 0.15, 1.0] Clear color, serialized but not in inspector ( camera.py:53,74 ). ## Usage in Editor Add Component → Camera. Pick Projection; for ortho set Ortho Size. Use Depth to order multiple cameras. Use Resolution Mode custom + Viewport Width/Height for fixed-size captures, otherwise render_scale for cheap previews. ## Usage in Code cam = entity.get_component(Camera) cam.fov = 55.0 cam.projection = CameraProjection.ORTHOGRAPHIC cam.ortho_size = 8.0 view = cam.get_view_matrix() proj = cam.get_projection_matrix(aspect=16.0 / 9.0) Related pages Editor Camera , Pipeline , Shadows Verified against core/components/rendering/cameras/camera.py:32-98 core/components/rendering/cameras/camera_base.py:12-111

docs.text: Directional Light Sun-style infinite light: DirectionalLight ( core/components/lighting/lightp/light.py:185-225 ) with lux intensity and optional procedural-sky driving. Home · Section index Overview Direction comes from the entity transform ( -forward is used by sky/cloud shaders). Intensity is illuminance in lux: direct sun 100000 , daylight 10000–25000 , overcast 1000–10000 , sunrise 400 , office 500 , twilight 10 , full moon 0.2 (inspector description + LUX_REFERENCE , light.py:40-48,198 ). docs.text: Light Base light component Light ( core/components/lighting/lightp/light.py ): color, physical intensity and shadow toggle; concrete types set units and extra fields. Home · Section index Overview LightType : directional / point / spot / area ; LightAreaType : rect / disk ( light.py:13-22 ). Base Light is editor-hidden ( _editor_hidden = True ); add a concrete type instead. Light.deserialize dispatches on light_type to DirectionalLight / PointLight / SpotLight / AreaLight ( light.py:147-161 ). Physical units: directional lux, point/spot lumens, area nits. Legacy scenes ( light_version < 2 ) are rescaled by LEGACY_DIRECTIONAL_MULT = 100000.0 , LEGACY_POINT_MULT = 2000.0 , LEGACY_AREA_MULT = 100.0 ( light.py:36-38 ). Properties name type default description color color3 [1.0, 1.0, 1.0] Light color ( light.py:72,78 ). intensity float (0–200000) 100000.0 Base default; concrete types override units ( light.py:73,79 ). cast_shadows bool True Enable shadow-map contribution ( light.py:74,80 ). ## Usage in Editor Add Directional/Point/Spot/Area Light (not base Light). White color + matching intensity presets from lux/lumen/nit references in code comments. Toggle cast_shadows off for fill lights. ## Usage in Code from core.components.lighting.lightp.light import DirectionalLight sun = entity.get_component(DirectionalLight) sun.color = [1.0, 0.95, 0.9] sun.intensity = 100000.0 sun.cast_shadows = True Related pages Directional Light , Point Light , Spot Light , Area Light , Shadows , Projector Verified against core/components/lighting/lightp/light.py:13-90,131-182

docs.text: Overview Forward OpenGL renderer: Renderer facade in core/renderer/renderer.py draws the scene into the viewport FBO in opaque then transparent phases. Home · Section index Overview ZarinEngine uses a forward renderer built on moderngl. Entry context is created in main.py : QSurfaceFormat , OpenGL 4.6 Core profile, depth buffer 24, swap interval from rendering.vsync ( 0 off / 1 on). Renderer composes mixins: config, programs, voxel, object-fx, framebuffers, water, uniforms, skinned, collector, geometry cache, outline, gizmo, icon, cubemap, post, scene ( core/renderer/renderer.py:56 ). Render modes are RenderMode.SHADED / SHADED_WIREFRAME / FLAT ( core/renderer/types.py ). Default caps: _max_lights = 8 , ambient [0.26, 0.28, 0.34] , selection outline [0.8, 0.5, 0.1, 1.0] thickness 0.03 ( core/renderer/renderer.py:90-114 ). Properties name type default description rendering.vsync bool (global config) True Swap interval 1 on / 0 off ( main.py:212 ). rendering.max_lights int (global config) 8 Size of u_lights[] uniform array ( core/renderer/rconfig/config_state.py:20 ). rendering.ambient vec3 (global config) [0.26, 0.28, 0.34] Fallback ambient ( core/renderer/renderer.py:112 ). render_mode RenderMode SHADED Shaded / shaded+wireframe / flat ( core/renderer/types.py ). ## Usage in Editor Viewport renders the active scene with the scene camera; grid, gizmos and outline are editor-only passes. docs.text: Pipeline Forward pipeline in SceneRendererMixin.render_scene : collect snapshot → shadow maps → opaque phase → transparent phase → environment (sky/water/clouds) → editor overlays. Home · Section index Overview render_scene(scene, view_mat, proj_mat, cam_pos, viewport_w, viewport_h, ...) ( core/renderer/scenev/mixin.py:24 ) applies _render_scale to get render size, collects a _RenderSnapshot (lights, dir_light , sky/cloud/water components, renderable entries), renders shadow maps via ShadowRenderer , then calls _scenev_render_forward_phases(opaque, transparent, ...) ( core/renderer/scenev/forward.py:19 ). Transparent phase enables SRC_ALPHA, ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA blending with depth_mask = False . Specialized passes: WaterPassMixin , VoxelPassMixin , SkinnedPassMixin , cubemap pass for dynamic reflections, GizmoPassMixin / IconPassMixin / OutlinePassMixin for the editor. Properties name type default description _render_scale float 1.0 Global render-size multiplier ( core/renderer/scenev/mixin.py:27 ). _shadow_resolution int per-light-type Shadow map size; see Shadows . _scene_fbo moderngl.Framebuffer None until init Scene color+depth target ( core/renderer/renderer.py:83-86 ). ## Usage in Editor Viewport size comes from the Qt viewport; per-camera render_scale / custom resolution further scales it (see Camera ). Stats overlay reads _draw_calls , _opaque_draws , _trans_draws , _triangles_drawn . ## Usage in Code renderer.render_scene(scene, cam.get_view_matrix(), cam.get_projection_matrix(aspect), cam_pos, 1280, 720) Related pages Overview , Camera , Shadows , Water , Gizmos Verified against core/renderer/scencev/mixin.py → core/renderer/scenev/mixin.py:24-80 core/renderer/scenev/forward.py:19-57 core/renderer/renderer.py:56-120 core/renderer/framebuffers.py , core/renderer/shadows/passes.py:183

docs.text: PostFX Stack Post-effects run in component order after the main scene pass. Each effect is a GraphicsEffect component with an enable toggle and its own Inspector fields. One page per effect: Bloom Blur Chromatic Aberration Color Grading Depth of Field Directional Blur Dithering Edge Detection Film Grain Fog FSR2 FXAA Glitch God Rays Hatching Kuwahara Lens Distortion Lens Flares Motion Blur Panini Pixelate Quantize Radial Blur Scanlines Sharpen Sobel SSAO SSR SVGF Vignette Watercolor Recipes: clean 3D (FXAA, Color Grading, Vignette), cinematic (Bloom, Depth of Field, Film Grain, Color Grading), retro (Pixelate, Scanlines, Dithering), horror (Fog, Vignette, Chromatic Aberration, Sharpen).

docs.text: Shadows Shadow-map system: ShadowRenderer ( core/renderer/shadows/renderer.py , passes.py:183 ) plus per-type quality owners DirectionalShadow / PointShadow / SpotShadow / AreaShadow . Home · Section index Overview render_shadow_pass(...) renders renderable_shadow casters into per-light maps: CSM for directional ( shadows/csm.py ), cube/dual maps for point ( shadows/point_spot.py ), perspective for spot, multi-sample for area ( shadows/area.py ), cookies for Projector ( shadows/projector.py ). Without an active owner component of a type, that type's shadows are disabled (headers in directional_shadow.py:7-9 , point_shadow.py:7-9 , spot_shadow.py:7-9 , area_shadow.py:7-9 ). Per-receiver flags: MeshRenderer.cast_shadows / receive_shadows . Properties name type default description DirectionalShadow._shadow_resolution int slider 256–4096 4096 Sun map size ( directional_shadow.py:33,45 ). DirectionalShadow._shadow_distance float slider 1–500 50.0 CSM range ( directional_shadow.py:35,46 ). DirectionalShadow._cascade_count int slider 1–4 4 Cascade count ( directional_shadow.py:37,58 ). DirectionalShadow._cascade_splits split gradient [0.05, 0.13, 0.3] Cascade boundaries for 4 cascades ( directional_shadow.py:18,39,47 ). PointShadow._shadow_resolution int slider 128–2048 512 Point map size ( point_shadow.py:31,37 ). SpotShadow._shadow_resolution int slider 128–2048 1024 Spot map size ( spot_shadow.py:31,37 ). AreaShadow._shadow_resolution int slider 128–2048 512 Area map size ( area_shadow.py:31,37 ). Light.cast_shadows bool True Per-light toggle (see light pages). ## Usage in Editor Add exactly one owner per type you use (e.g. Directional Shadow). Raise Resolution for crisp edges, shorten Shadow Distance to concentrate CSM texels, use 2–3 cascades for small scenes and 4 for open worlds. ## Usage in Code ds = entity.get_component(DirectionalShadow) ds._shadow_resolution = 2048 ds._shadow_distance = 120.0 Related pages Light , Directional Light , Point Light , Spot Light , Area Light , Mesh Renderer Verified against core/renderer/shadows/passes.py:59,183 core/renderer/shadows/csm.py , point_spot.py , area.py , projector.py:28 core/components/rendering/environment/directional_shadow.py:28-48 core/components/rendering/environment/point_shadow.py:26-37 core/components/rendering/environment/spot_shadow.py:26-37 core/components/rendering/environment/area_shadow.py:26-37

docs.text: Dissolve Noise-gradient burn-off. Fragments past amount (biased by directional gradient × noise_strength + noise field × noise_scale) are discarded; a band of width edge_width glows with edge_color × edge_emission. Optional time animation drives amount 0→1 (ping-pong or loop). Class DissolveEffect in core/components/rendering/effects/dissolve_effect.py . ObjectFx pass ( core/renderer/object_fx_pass.py ): enabled DissolveEffect components are collected per entity ( _find_object_effect ) and bound in the FX program before the mesh draw. Parameters Inspector Field Type Range Default Amount amount SLIDER 0.0 – 1.0 0.0 Noise Strength noise_strength SLIDER 0.0 – 1.0 1.0 Noise Scale noise_scale FLOAT 0.1 – 20.0 4.0 Gradient Direction direction VEC3 -1.0 – 1.0 (0.0, 1.0, 0.0) Invert invert BOOL — False Edge Width edge_width SLIDER 0.0 – 0.5 0.05 Edge Color edge_color COLOR — [1.0, 0.4, 0.05] Edge Emission edge_emission SLIDER 0.0 – 5.0 2.5 Animate animate BOOL — False Speed speed FLOAT 0.0 – 5.0 0.5 Ping Pong ping_pong BOOL — False Usage Editor: select the mesh entity, Add Component > DissolveEffect , tick enabled , animate the amount fields from a script. Code: from core.components.rendering.effects.dissolve_effect import DissolveEffect fx = DissolveEffect() entity.add_component(fx) fx.amount = 0.5 fx.edge_width = 0.08 fx.animate = True fx.enabled = True # per-frame: fx.amount = min(1.0, fx.amount + dt * 0.5) Shader snippet Shader: core/shaders/internal/ObjectFx.shader (u_dissolve_* branch) + dissolve_effect.py::_apply . Bound uniforms: u_dissolve_amount , u_dissolve_edge , u_dissolve_color , u_dissolve_edge_emission , u_dissolve_noise_scale , u_dissolve_noise_strength , u_dissolve_dir , u_dissolve_invert , u_time . // dissolve_effect.py::_apply (exact uniform names): // prog["u_dissolve_amount"] = float(amount) // prog["u_dissolve_edge"] = float(edge_width) // prog["u_dissolve_color"] = vec3(edge_color) // prog["u_dissolve_edge_emission"], prog["u_dissolve_noise_scale"], prog["u_dissolve_noise_strength"], prog["u_dissolve_dir"], prog["u_dissolve_invert"] Related Related: Object Effects , ObjectFx pass ( core/renderer/object_fx_pass.py ), core/shaders/internal/ObjectFx.shader . docs.text: Frost Directional ice coverage. Freeze gradient along direction mixes ice color by coverage × amount; crack pattern scale sets fracture frequency; sparkle adds view glints; rim_power shapes the fresnel rim. Optional animate flag. docs.text: Voxel Raymarch Mesh→volume raymarch. Host mesh is voxelized on CPU into a 3D texture (dims clamped to 192 max), then a fullscreen pass raymarches (max_steps) with Beer-Lambert-ish alpha × opacity × amount, shaded by color/emission/rim and light_dir. Blends with SRC_ALPHA/ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA over the scene color target. Class VoxelRaymarchEffect in core/components/rendering/effects/voxelp/effect.py . NOTE: despite living under effects/, this is a GraphicsEffect (fullscreen raymarch into a 3D occupancy texture), not an ObjectEffect. Requires a MeshFilter on the same entity to build the grid; disabled/fast-pathed when amount/opacity ≤ 0.001. docs.text: Light Units Physical units per light type — lux for directional, lumens for point/spot, nits for area — the in-code reference tables, legacy multipliers, and a setup guide. Home · Section index Overview Base class Light ( core/components/lighting/lightp/light.py:25-90 ) stores color , intensity (0–200000), and cast_shadows . Units depend on the concrete type: DirectionalLight reads lux, PointLight / SpotLight read lumens, AreaLight reads nits. Internal conversion factors are LUX_TO_RADIANCE = 1e-5 , CANDELA_TO_RADIANCE = 1e-2 , AREA_TO_RADIANCE = 1e-2 ( light.py:33-35 ). Properties name type default description DirectionalLight.intensity float, lux 100000.0 Illuminance in lux ( light.py:198,205 ). PointLight.intensity float, lumens 1000.0 Total flux in lumens ( light.py:241,248 ). SpotLight.intensity float, lumens in cone 1000.0 Same lumens concentrated by the cone angle ( light.py:317,327 ). AreaLight.intensity float, nits 100.0 Surface brightness in cd/m² ( shadows.py:92,106 ). Light.color color3 [1,1,1] Light color ( light.py:72,78 ). Light.cast_shadows bool True Shadow-map contribution ( light.py:74,80 ). Reference tables (verbatim keys, light.py:40-64 ) LUX_REFERENCE : direct_sun 100000.0 , full_daylight 15000.0 , overcast_day 5000.0 , sunrise_sunset 400.0 , office 500.0 , twilight 10.0 , full_moon 0.2 . LUMEN_REFERENCE : candle 12.57 , decorative_led 100.0 , desk_lamp 300.0 , room_ceiling 800.0 , bulb_100w 1600.0 , street_light 15000.0 , stadium_floodlight 100000.0 . NIT_REFERENCE : monitor_sdr 200.0 , office_panel 500.0 , overcast_sky 2000.0 , clear_sky 5000.0 , led_softbox 10000.0 . Setup guide Sun : DirectionalLight , intensity = 100000.0 (direct sun). Overcast day 5000 , sunrise 400 . Bulb/lamp : PointLight , intensity = 1000.0 (≈100 W bulb is 1600 lm; desk lamp 300 lm). Set range to the room size. Flashlight/spot : SpotLight , intensity = 1000.0 ; narrow cones look brighter because the same lumens are concentrated. Softbox/panel : AreaLight , intensity = 100.0 default; office panel ≈ 500 nits, LED softbox ≈ 10000 nits. Bigger panels emit more total light at equal nits. Fill lights : switch cast_shadows off. Legacy migration Scenes with light_version < 2 are auto-rescaled ( light.py:36-38,166-167 ): LEGACY_DIRECTIONAL_MULT = 100000.0 , LEGACY_POINT_MULT = 2000.0 (also applied to spot), LEGACY_AREA_MULT = 100.0 . New scenes serialize light_version: 2 ( light.py:134 ). docs.text: Material Library Every shipped material asset under assets/materials/ (currently a single .mat file), the .mat JSON field table from core/assets/matp/materials.py , and a verbatim example. Home · Section index Overview Material assets are .mat JSON files ( Material { name, shader_path, properties } ), loaded by Material ( core/assets/matp/materials.py:14-169 ) and cached by MaterialManager ( core/renderer/mats/manager.py:54-80 ). shader_path = "default" maps to the built-in PBR; any other path is resolved against the project root first, then engine core/shaders/ ( materials.py:26-46 ). Missing files warn once and fall back to default ( manager.py:63-71 ). No .zpem files ship under assets/ at time of writing. Listing ( assets/materials/ ) file material shader purpose ProBuilderPrototype.mat ProBuilderPrototype default (built-in PBR) Grey prototype grid texture for blockout geometry ( albedo_texture: ../textures/prototype_texture.png ). .mat JSON fields field type default description name string "" Material name ( materials.py:14-24 ). shader_path string "default" .shader path or "default" for built-in PBR ( materials.py:48-52,110-118 ). Non- .shader extensions are rejected when loading shader properties. properties object {} Shader uniforms ( manager.py:89-96 ). Missing keys are back-filled from the shader's Properties defaults ( materials.py:63-66 ). Shader resolution order for a non-default path ( materials.py:26-46 ): absolute path if it exists → <project_root>/<path> → <engine_root>/<path> → <engine_root>/core/shaders/<path> → basename lookup inside materials/ , internal/ , compute/ , include/ , legacy/ . Example (verbatim) assets/materials/ProBuilderPrototype.mat : {"name": "ProBuilderPrototype", "properties": {"_BaseColor": [1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0], "_EmissionColor": [0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0], "_EmissionIntensity": 0.0, "_Metallic": 0.0, "_Smoothness": 0.5, "albedo_texture": "../textures/prototype_texture.png"}, "shader_path": "default"} Usage in Editor Create a .mat file in Assets, pick a Shader, edit the exposed Properties . Assign the file to Mesh Renderer material slots. Usage in Code from core.assets.matp import Material m = Material.load("assets/materials/ProBuilderPrototype.mat", project_root) m.set_property("_Metallic", 0.2) m.save("assets/materials/ProBuilderPrototype.mat", project_root) Related pages Materials , Shaders , Shader Catalog , Mesh Renderer Verified against assets/materials/ProBuilderPrototype.mat (verbatim above; sole .mat under assets/ ; no .zpem files under assets/ ) core/assets/matp/materials.py:14-70 ( Material , _resolve_shader_path , load_shader_properties , save ) core/renderer/mats/manager.py:54-100

docs.text: PostFX Stack Order The exact frame order — snapshot → shadow pass → opaque/transparent forward phases → additive effects → screen-effect chain → tonemap hook — how to order effects, and how the tonemapping hook works. Home · Section index Overview One frame in SceneRendererMixin.render_scene ( core/renderer/scenev/mixin.py:24 ) runs in this order: Snapshot — _collect_snapshot(scene, ...) ( mixin.py:54 ) gathers lights, sky, renderable entries, sprites, videos, SVGs, particles into a _RenderSnapshot . Shadow pass — _scenev_render_shadow_pass(...) ( mixin.py:144 ) renders CSM/point/spot/area shadow maps. Skybox + forward phases — sky render ( mixin.py:158 ), then _scenev_partition_and_sort splits opaque vs transparent ( mixin.py:204 ) and _scenev_render_forward_phases draws opaque first, transparent second ( core/renderer/scenev/forward.py:19-34 ). Additive effects — every GraphicsEffect with render_type != "screen" renders directly into the scene FBO ( output.py:269-281 ). Screen-effect chain — render_type == "screen" effects run ping-pong between _se_fbo_a / _se_fbo_b in registry order ( output.py:285-324 ). Tonemap hook — _present_composite ( post_pass.py:28-44 ) presents the composite texture. How to order effects Execution order inside each group (additive, screen) is GraphicsEffect._registry order — i.e. component creation/enable order ( graphics_effect.py:16,39-54 ). There is no numeric priority field; reorder by re-adding components or toggling enabled / entity.active . render_type is a class attribute ( graphics_effect.py:18 ): most postfx (bloom excluded) use "screen" ; Bloom and lens-flare style effects use "additive" and run before the screen chain. Skipped effects cost nothing: should_skip() ( graphics_effect.py:28-37 ) drops disabled/inactive entities and any effect whose _intensity_prop is <= 0.001 (plus _skip_rate frame skipping). Tonemapping hook PostPassMixin._has_tonemap_effect ( post_pass.py:18-25 ): def _has_tonemap_effect(self): if not GraphicsEffect._registry: return False from core.components.rendering.postfx.color_grading import ColorGrading for e in GraphicsEffect._registry: if isinstance(e, ColorGrading) and e.enabled and e.entity and e.entity.active: return True return False _present_composite ( post_pass.py:28-44 ): if a live ColorGrading effect exists (or the tonemap program is missing), the plain copy program is used — tonemapping is then owned by ColorGrading in the screen chain. Otherwise the built-in tonemap program runs with u_exposure from self._exposure . Properties name type default description GraphicsEffect.render_type "additive" / "screen" "additive" Which group the effect runs in ( graphics_effect.py:18 ). GraphicsEffect._intensity_prop string "" Auto-skip knob; effect skipped when <= 0.001 ( graphics_effect.py:32-36 ). GraphicsEffect._skip_rate int 0 Render every N+1-th frame when > 0 ( graphics_effect.py:29-31 ). renderer._exposure float 0.0 Exposure fed to u_exposure only on the built-in tonemap path ( renderer.py:172 , post_pass.py:41 ). Usage in Code fx.enabled = True # include in the chain fx.render_type # "screen" -> ping-pong chain, "additive" -> scene FBO GraphicsEffect._registry # order == execution order within each group Related pages PostFX Stack , Color Grading , Pipeline Verified against core/renderer/scenev/mixin.py:24-210 ( render_scene : snapshot :54 , shadow pass :144 , partition :204 , forward :209 ) core/renderer/scenev/forward.py:19-34 (opaque then transparent phases) core/renderer/scenev/output.py:207-330 ( _scenev_render_effects : additive :269-281 , screen ping-pong :285-324 , _present_composite :326 ) core/renderer/post_pass.py:18-44 ( _has_tonemap_effect , _present_composite ) core/components/rendering/postfx/graphics_effect.py:15-37 ( _registry , render_type , should_skip )

docs.text: Raytracing Setup Raytracing.compute kernel contract, component knobs, hard limits, and performance guidance. Home · Section index Overview The path-tracer is a #version 430 core compute kernel ( local_size 8×8 , core/shaders/compute/Raytracing.compute:13-15 ) driven by the RaytraceRenderer component split across core/components/rendering/renderers/raytrace/ ( component.py , dispatch.py , denoise.py ). Kernel properties (verbatim, Raytracing.compute:3-11 ) Properties { _MaxBounces("Max Bounces", Int) = 1 _SamplesPerPixel("Samples Per Pixel", Int) = 1 _ResolutionScale("Resolution Scale", Float) = 1.0 _Accumulate("Accumulate Frames", Int) = 0 _HeatmapMode("Heatmap Mode", Int) = 0 _HeatmapScale("Heatmap Scale", Float) = 40.0 } Hard GLSL limits ( Raytracing.compute:17-18 ): #define MAX_INSTANCES 256 , #define MAX_LIGHTS 8 . Extra instances/lights are dropped during scene upload ( denoise.py:85,217-243 ). Component knobs ( raytrace/component.py:31-49 ) field range default description _resolution_scale 0.1–1.0 0.5 Trace resolution factor; dispatch size max(1, size × scale) ( dispatch.py:17-18 ). _max_bounces 1–16 1 → u_max_bounces . _samples_per_pixel 1–16 1 → u_samples_per_pixel . _accumulate bool False → u_accumulate ; progressive refine ( dispatch.py:126 ). _show_overlay bool True Composite overlay presentation. _heatmap_mode 0–2 0 → u_heatmap_mode (off/cost diagnostic). _heatmap_scale 1–256 40.0 → u_heatmap_scale . Buffers bound at dispatch: BVH nodes (0), vertices (1), indices (2), materials (3), instances (4), lights (5), plus rgba32f output/emissive images and a 32-layer albedo texture array ( _MAX_ALBEDO_LAYERS = 32 , component.py:17 , dispatch.py:79 ). Requirements OpenGL 4.3+ compute (SSBO + image load/store, #version 430 core ). Scene caps: 256 instances, 8 lights, 32 albedo layers — components beyond the cap are ignored with no error besides the drop. Rays/frame accounting: rw × rh × spp × (bounces + 1) ( dispatch.py:271 , surfaced as _rt_rays_per_frame ). Performance notes Cost scales linearly with pixels (× resolution_scale² ), spp, and bounces+1. Start at 0.5 scale / 1 bounce / 1 spp, enable _accumulate for stills, and use _heatmap_mode to find hot spots before raising quality. Usage in Code rt._resolution_scale = 0.5 rt._max_bounces = 1 rt._samples_per_pixel = 1 rt._accumulate = False Related pages Raytracing Renderer , Shader Catalog , Pipeline Verified against core/shaders/compute/Raytracing.compute:1-60 (Properties, #version 430 , local_size 8×8 , MAX_INSTANCES 256 , MAX_LIGHTS 8 , uniforms) core/components/rendering/renderers/raytrace/component.py:14-49,95-121 (limits, knobs, defaults, serialization) core/components/rendering/renderers/raytrace/dispatch.py:17-18,124-160,271-294 (scale, uniforms, ray count, overlay) core/components/rendering/renderers/raytrace/denoise.py:85,217-260 (cap enforcement)

docs.text: Shadows Tuning Resolution/distance/cascade defaults per light type, bias constants, and performance notes — all from code. Home · Section index Overview Shadow settings have two layers: the DirectionalShadow scene component (authored values) and renderer fallbacks ( core/renderer/renderer.py:125-131 ) used when no component is present. The shadow backend is ShadowRenderer ( core/renderer/shadows/renderer.py:23-30 ). Properties setting authored default ( DirectionalShadow ) renderer fallback code Directional resolution 4096 2048 directional_shadow.py:45 , renderer.py:125 Shadow distance 50.0 m 50.0 m directional_shadow.py:46 , renderer.py:126 Cascades 4 4 directional_shadow.py:48 , renderer.py:127 Cascade splits (4) [0.05, 0.13, 0.3] computed log/linear blend ( lam = 0.9 ) directional_shadow.py:18 , csm.py:69-75 Point resolution — 512 renderer.py:129 Area resolution — 512 renderer.py:130 Spot resolution — 1024 renderer.py:131 u_shadow_bias — 0.0015 shadows/uniforms.py:213 u_shadow_normal_bias — 0.02 shadows/uniforms.py:214 area_shadow_bias 0.005 (per AreaLight ) 0.005 light.py:90 , shadows/area.py:71-73 Cascade tile resolutions for a 4-cascade map derive from the base: [base, max(512, base//2), max(512, base//2), max(256, base//4)] ( shadows/uniforms.py:33 ), with a static atlas layout of [2048, 1024, 1024, 512] in the renderer ( shadows/renderer.py:70 ). Tuning guide Directional : resolution slider 256–4096 step 256, distance 1–500 m, cascades 1–4 ( directional_shadow.py:33-40 ). 4096 + 4 cascades is the authored default; drop to 2048/2 cascades for low-end. Splits : defaults per count are {2: [0.5], 3: [0.2, 0.6], 4: [0.05, 0.13, 0.3]} ( directional_shadow.py:18 , mirrored in editor/cascade_split_widget.py:15 ). Push splits outward to cover far ground, inward for close-up detail. Point/spot/area : fixed at 512/1024/512 in the renderer; disable cast_shadows on fill lights instead of lowering globally. Acne vs peter-panning : raise u_shadow_bias / u_shadow_normal_bias against acne; raise area_shadow_bias (0–0.1, step 0.001) per area light ( shadows.py:100 ). Performance notes Shadow cost scales with cascade count × tile resolution plus one 512² cube-ish pass per point light and one 1024² pass per spot. ShadowRenderer clamps cascades to 1–4 ( shadows/renderer.py:25 ). Outline queue rendering is capped at 512 entries ( output.py:397 ). Usage in Code from core.components.rendering.environment.directional_shadow import DirectionalShadow ds = DirectionalShadow() ds._shadow_resolution = 4096 ds._shadow_distance = 50.0 ds._set_cascade_count(4) Related pages Shadows , Directional Light , Light Units Verified against core/components/rendering/environment/directional_shadow.py:18-48 (splits table, 4096/50.0/4 defaults, sliders) core/renderer/renderer.py:125-133 (2048/50.0/4 + 512/512/1024 fallbacks, type flags) core/renderer/shadows/renderer.py:23-30,46-70 (constructor, clamp, _cascade_resolutions ) core/renderer/shadows/csm.py:54-75 (split computation, lam = 0.9 ) core/renderer/shadows/uniforms.py:29-47,213-214,294 (settings update, biases) core/renderer/shadows/area.py:71-73 , core/components/lighting/lightp/light.py:90

docs.text: Splat Pipeline Gaussian splat ingest → GPU upload → sorted rasterization: supported formats, SH degree, opacity cutoff, GL requirements, and the _splat_sort sorter. Home · Section index Overview GaussianSplatRenderer ( core/components/rendering/renderers/gaussian_splat_renderer.py:12-35 ) points at a splat file and tunes evaluation. The GPU backend is _SplatResourcesMixin ( core/renderer/splat/resources.py:330-388 ); sorting uses the optional Cython core._splat_sort module ( core/renderer/splat/sort.py:31-34 , built in core/build_cython.py:127 ). Properties name type default description ply_path resource path "" Splat file; picker filter Splats (*.ply *.sog *.ssog) ( gaussian_splat_renderer.py:23-24 ). sh_degree int slider 0–3 3 Spherical-harmonics degree uploaded as u_sh_degree ( gaussian_splat_renderer.py:25-26 , resources.py:385-386 ). opacity_threshold float 0–1 0.005 Opacity cutoff uploaded as u_opacity_threshold ( gaussian_splat_renderer.py:27-28 , resources.py:387-388 ). Formats and import _is_sog_style ( resources.py:306-313 ) treats these as directory/archive-style splats: .sog , .ssog , .zip , paths ending in /meta.json or /lod-meta.json , or basenames meta.json / lod-meta.json . Everything else goes through _load_splat_file ( resources.py:316-327 ): the first 4 lines are sniffed — binary PLY takes the fast path ( _load_splat_fast ), otherwise the generic loader ( _load_splat_generic ). Relative ply_path values resolve against the project root with an assets/ fallback ( post_pass.py:47-61 ). GPU requirements and sorting Shader init failure logs GaussianSplatRenderer shader init failed (needs OpenGL 4.3+): ... and disables the program/VAO ( resources.py:342-345 ). SSBO storage buffers are used ( _ensure_buffers , _bind_gpu_draw binding points 0–1). Per-frame uniforms: u_model , u_view , u_proj , u_viewport , u_camera_pos , u_sh_degree , u_opacity_threshold ( resources.py:369-388 ). Sorting uses splat_cull_depth , compact_keep , radix_sort_into , remap_order from core._splat_sort when compiled, with a NumPy fallback ( splat/sort.py:31-34,168 ). Usage in Code from core.components.rendering.renderers.gaussian_splat_renderer import GaussianSplatRenderer gs = GaussianSplatRenderer() gs.ply_path = "assets/splats/scan.ply" gs.sh_degree = 3 gs.opacity_threshold = 0.005 entity.add_component(gs) Related pages Gaussian Splat Renderer , Pipeline Verified against core/components/rendering/renderers/gaussian_splat_renderer.py:19-53 (fields, defaults, serialization) core/renderer/splat/resources.py:300-388 (SOG detection, loader dispatch, GL 4.3+ message at :343 , SSBO buffers, uniforms) core/renderer/splat/sort.py:31-34 , core/build_cython.py:127 ( core._splat_sort ) core/renderer/post_pass.py:47-61 ( _gaussian_ply_path resolution)

docs.text: Voxel Pipeline Object voxelization ( VoxelizeEffect ), the voxel_pass instancing backend with its hard caps, and the screen-space VoxelRaymarchEffect . Home · Section index Overview Two components cover voxels: VoxelizeEffect (an ObjectEffect that voxelizes the host mesh) and VoxelRaymarchEffect (a GraphicsEffect that raymarches a 3D occupancy texture). Instanced voxel cubes are drawn by VoxelPassMixin ( core/renderer/voxel_pass.py:18-25 ). VoxelizeEffect ( core/components/rendering/effects/voxelize_effect.py:18-52 ) name type default description amount slider 0–1 0.5 Blend between base mesh and voxels. show_base_mesh bool True Keep drawing the original mesh. world_grid bool False Snap voxels to a world grid instead of object space. voxel_size float 0.3 Target voxel size; also cell = 0.3 . scale vec3 [1,1,1] Per-voxel cube scale. jitter float 0.0 Cell jitter seed factor. emission float 2.5 Voxel glow. color color3 [0.4, 1.0, 0.6] Voxel tint. rim float 2.5 Rim power. double_sided bool True Two-sided voxel cubes. animate / speed_anim / ping_pong bool / float / bool False / 0.5 / False Auto-animate amount 0→1. Voxel cells are computed on CPU by compute_voxel_instances and cached per (mesh, size, grid, jitter) key ( voxelize_effect.py:59-72 ). voxel_pass caps ( core/renderer/voxel_pass.py:22-25 ) constant value meaning _VOX_MAX_DIM 128 Max grid dimension; larger extents rescale the cell ( voxel_pass.py:304-309 ). _VOX_MAX_INSTANCES 2200000 Instance clamp: need_inst = min(total, _VOX_MAX_INSTANCES) ( voxel_pass.py:164 ). The instanced vertex shader ( _VOXEL_INST_VERT , #version 330 core ) packs i_cell.xyz (center) + i_cell.w (cull flag) with u_vox_size / u_vox_scale . VoxelRaymarchEffect ( core/components/rendering/effects/voxelp/effect.py:22-59 ) A GraphicsEffect ( render_type = "additive" , _intensity_prop = "amount" , multi-instance allowed) rendering a fullscreen raymarch over a texture3d occupancy grid built from the host MeshFilter . name type default description amount slider 0–1 1.0 Effect intensity (auto-skipped at <= 0.001 ). voxel_size float 0.3 Grid cell size. color color3 [0.4, 1.0, 0.6] Voxel color. emission float 0.6 Glow. rim float 2.5 Rim power. opacity slider 0–1 1.0 Output opacity. max_steps int 32–1024 256 Raymarch steps. light_dir vec3 [0.4, 0.8, 0.3] March lighting direction. Grid build cap: max_dim = 192 — if ceil(extent / cell) exceeds it, the cell is enlarged to max(extent) / 192 ( effect.py:164-167 ). Usage in Code from core.components.rendering.effects.voxelize_effect import VoxelizeEffect vx = VoxelizeEffect() vx.amount = 0.5 vx.voxel_size = 0.3 entity.add_component(vx) Related pages Voxelize , Voxel Raymarch , Voxel Rendering , Object Effects Verified against core/components/rendering/effects/voxelize_effect.py:18-152 (defaults, serializer, inspector) core/renderer/voxel_pass.py:18-25,164,304-309 ( _VOX_MAX_DIM = 128 , _VOX_MAX_INSTANCES = 2200000 ) core/components/rendering/effects/voxelp/effect.py:22-91,156-185 ( VoxelRaymarchEffect , max_dim = 192 , max_steps = 256 ) core/renderer/object_fx_pass.py:15,114 (voxel effect hook)

docs.text: Cython in Scripts Heavy computations move to a Cython module next to the plain script — no manual build steps, no polluted script folders. Setup: Project → Create → Cython Script creates fast_sum.pyx with a working template. A plain script in the same folder writes import fast_sum . Before import, the engine prepares the script folder on the module search path, then on first import compiles the extension into cache/cython automatically. On Windows the bundled MinGW toolchain is discovered by the engine itself. import move_fast class Mover: speed: float = 5.0 def on_update(self, dt): step = move_fast.clamp_step(self.speed * dt, 0.0, 1.0) t = self._entity.transform if t: t.translate(Vec3(0.0, 0.0, step)) cpdef double clamp_step(double value, double lo, double hi): if value < lo: return lo if value > hi: return hi return value Rules and mechanics: The module name is top-level: import foo where foo.pyx sits next to the script. Names must be unique within the project. A neighboring foo.pxd declaration file is tracked for rebuilds too. Rebuilds are automatic when the .pyx (or .pxd ) is newer than the cached build. Artifacts live in cache/cython under build/<dirhash16>/<fingerprint12> (directory hash + 12-hex source fingerprint over .pyx , neighboring .pxd , Cython version and toolchain); only the last 3 builds per script folder are kept. The script folder stays clean. Editing .pyx during Play triggers a script hot-reload as usual. The Check button validates .pyx without a C compiler (Cython parsing and typing only). The full native build happens lazily on first import. If no compiler is found, the console shows an actionable error and the script keeps working on the previous working build — iteration never hard-blocks on toolchain setup. Keep the Python/Cython boundary typed ( cpdef , typed locals) and batch calls: one call processing an array beats per-element calls across the boundary. When to reach for it: per-frame math over many elements (crowds, particles logic, procedural deformation), tight loops the profiler attributes to a script, and numeric kernels. Game flow, input and orchestration stay in plain Python. Troubleshooting: stale results → touch the .pyx (mtime drives rebuilds); import errors → module name collision within the project, rename uniquely; slow first Play → that is the one-time compile, later runs reuse cache/cython .

docs.text: Script Examples Copy-paste behaviors. All run as-is: create a Python Script asset, replace its content, attach to an entity, press Play. Rotator — spins around Y using the frame delta: from core.maths.math3d import Vec3 class Rotator: speed: float = 90.0 def on_update(self, dt): t = self._entity.get_component_by_name("Transform") if t: t.rotate(Vec3(0.0, self.speed * dt, 0.0)) Mover — constant forward motion with an Inspector slider: from typing import Annotated from core.maths.math3d import Vec3 class Mover: speed: Annotated[float, Range(0.0, 20.0)] = 5.0 def on_update(self, dt): t = self._entity.transform if t: t.translate(Vec3(0.0, 0.0, self.speed * dt)) Keyboard driver — WASD movement plus sprint on Shift: from core.maths.math3d import Vec3 class Driver: speed: float = 6.0 sprint: float = 10.0 def on_update(self, dt): v = Vec3(0.0, 0.0, 0.0) if Input.GetKey(KeyCode.W): v = v + Vec3(0.0, 0.0, 1.0) if Input.GetKey(KeyCode.S): v = v + Vec3(0.0, 0.0, -1.0) if Input.GetKey(KeyCode.A): v = v + Vec3(-1.0, 0.0, 0.0) if Input.GetKey(KeyCode.D): v = v + Vec3(1.0, 0.0, 0.0) rate = self.sprint if (Input.GetKey(KeyCode.LEFT_SHIFT) or Input.GetKey(KeyCode.RIGHT_SHIFT)) else self.speed t = self._entity.transform if t and v.length() > 0.0: t.translate(v.normalized() * rate * dt) Patrol — waypoint ping-pong with an enum mode and a cached Transform: from enum import Enum from core.maths.math3d import Vec3 class PatrolMode(Enum): PINGPONG = 0 LOOP = 1 class Patrol: mode: PatrolMode = PatrolMode.PINGPONG speed: float = 3.0 distance: float = 8.0 def on_awake(self): self.t = self._entity.transform self.home = Vec3(0.0, 0.0, 0.0) self.dir = 1.0 if self.t: self.home = self.t.position def on_update(self, dt): if not self.t: return step = self.speed * self.dir * dt self.t.translate(Vec3(step, 0.0, 0.0)) walked = self.t.position.x - self.home.x if self.mode == PatrolMode.LOOP: if walked > self.distance or walked < 0.0: self.t.position = Vec3(self.home.x, self.t.position.y, self.t.position.z) else: if walked > self.distance or walked < 0.0: self.dir = -self.dir Follower — chase an Entity picked in the Inspector: from core.maths.math3d import Vec3 class Follower: target: 'Entity' = None speed: float = 4.0 stop_at: float = 1.5 def on_update(self, dt): if not self.target: return t = self._entity.transform goal = self.target.transform if not t or not goal: return delta = goal.position - t.position dist = delta.length() if dist > self.stop_at: t.translate(delta.normalized() * self.speed * dt) Hit counter — collision callbacks with impact force and an Inspector button: class HitCounter: hits: int = 0 last_force: float = 0.0 _inspector_buttons = [("reset", "Reset")] def on_collision_enter(self, other_id, force): self.hits = self.hits + 1 self.last_force = force def reset(self): self.hits = 0 self.last_force = 0.0 Physics kick — impulse on key press for an entity with Rigidbody: from core.maths.math3d import Vec3 class Kicker: impulse: float = 5.0 def on_update(self, dt): if Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.SPACE): rb = self._entity.get_component_by_name("Rigidbody") if rb: rb.add_impulse(Vec3(0.0, self.impulse, 0.0)) Countdown spawner — timed logic with enable/disable safety: class Spawner: interval: float = 2.0 active: bool = True def on_awake(self): self.clock = 0.0 self.count = 0 def on_update(self, dt): if not self.active: return self.clock = self.clock + dt if self.clock >= self.interval: self.clock = 0.0 self.count = self.count + 1 Logger.info("spawn tick") def on_disable(self): self.clock = 0.0

docs.text: Hot Reload A script file can be edited while Play is running. The change is picked up on the next frame: the instance is recreated, Inspector values are preserved, and on_awake / on_start run again. Instance state from __init__ is reset, like a recompilation in Unity. Reload pipeline: The engine compares the file modification time before each on_update / on_fixed_update . A newer mtime starts a reload. The file is re-validated (same checks as the Check button). On errors a single consolidated console message Script '...' has N error(s): is written per file version, and the previous working instance keeps running. On success the module re-executes with the injected API, the behavior class is re-resolved, and a fresh instance is constructed. Inspector field values are re-applied onto the new instance, then on_awake and on_start run again. What survives: Inspector-tuned values, the component wiring, the entity hierarchy. What resets: anything assigned in __init__ or built up in callbacks (timers, caches, spawned handles) — rebuild it in on_awake / on_start if the behavior must continue seamlessly. The Check button validates without Play in three stages: syntax parse with file:line positions, core.* import resolution (including the hint to use core.maths.math3d instead of core.math3d ), and a full trial execution catching runtime import errors such as circular imports. Control: the hot_reload flag on ScriptComponent (default True ). Set False to freeze the instance for the session — useful when debugging native-side state or comparing against a fixed baseline. Workflow tips: keep Play running and iterate on feel (speeds, curves, timings) with an external editor; the tuned Inspector values persist across reloads, so save the scene when the feel is right. For structural refactors (renamed fields, new buttons) expect one clean reload cycle and re-check the Inspector. Troubleshooting: changes ignored → the file did not save (mtime unchanged) or hot_reload is off; old behavior persists with errors → fix the reported file:line entries, the last working build stays live meanwhile; fields reset → the annotation was renamed, the old stored value has no target.

docs.text: Input and Math API These names are injected into every user script module automatically, so importing them is optional. An explicit import with the same name in the script takes priority over the injection. Injected names: Input , KeyCode , Vec2 , Vec3 , Vec4 , Curve , Range , Logger . Keyboard and mouse: Input.GetKey(code) — held this frame; Input.GetKeyDown(code) — pressed this frame; Input.GetKeyUp(code) — released this frame. Codes come from KeyCode ( KeyCode.W , KeyCode.SPACE , KeyCode.LEFT_SHIFT / KeyCode.RIGHT_SHIFT , arrows, digits and more). Input.GetMouseButton(i) , GetMouseButtonDown(i) , GetMouseButtonUp(i) — button index state. Input.GetButton(name) , GetButtonDown(name) , GetButtonUp(name) — named action buttons. Input.GetAxis(name) , Input.GetAxisRaw(name) — smoothed vs raw axes such as "Horizontal" . Input.mousePosition — cursor in screen space; Input.deltaTime — scaled frame time; Input.cursorLocked / Input.cursorVisible — pointer capture state. Math: Vec2 , Vec3 , Vec4 — full vector math (add, scale, dot, cross, length, normalized, lerp) backed by numpy.float64 ; the GPU downgrade to float32 happens only on upload. Quat , Mat4 — import from core.maths.math3d for rotations and matrices (slerp, look_at, perspective helpers live there with numba acceleration). Curve — keyframed response curves edited in the Inspector and evaluated at runtime for falloff, easing and throttle shapes. Range — slider metadata for Inspector fields (see Inspector Fields). Logger — Logger.info/warning/error with timestamps; errors include tracebacks and reach the console panel. Frame-rate independence: always multiply motion by dt (or use Input.deltaTime ); fixed-step logic belongs in on_fixed_update with its stable step. class Player: speed: float = 6.0 def on_update(self, dt): step = self.speed * dt t = self._entity.transform if Input.GetKey(KeyCode.W): t.translate(Vec3(0.0, 0.0, step)) if Input.GetKey(KeyCode.S): t.translate(Vec3(0.0, 0.0, -step)) if Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.SPACE): Logger.info("jump pressed") class Looker: sensitivity: float = 2.0 def on_update(self, dt): x = Input.GetAxis("Horizontal") t = self._entity.transform if t and x != 0.0: t.rotate(Vec3(0.0, x * self.sensitivity * dt, 0.0)) Cursor pattern for fly cameras: lock on right-mouse hold, release on up — drive Input.cursorLocked from the mouse-button callbacks in on_update . Axes such as "Horizontal" exist only after bindings are loaded ( Input.LoadProjectBindings at startup) or an explicit Input.DefineAxis("Horizontal", positive=[KeyCode.D], negative=[KeyCode.A]) . An undefined axis name makes GetAxis / GetAxisRaw return 0.0 , so the Looker above stays still until the axis is defined — define it in project setup before relying on it (see Input overview).

docs.text: Inspector Fields and Range Annotated class attributes automatically appear in the Inspector, and their values are stored in the scene ( .zpes ). Class-level defaults become the initial values; per-instance edits override them without touching the .py file. Private names starting with _ are skipped, except the special _inspector_buttons . from enum import Enum from typing import Annotated from core.maths.math3d import Vec3 from core.foundation.curve import Curve class Mode(Enum): IDLE = 0 PATROL = 1 class Enemy: speed: Annotated[float, Range(0.0, 10.0)] = 5.0 health: int = 100 title: str = "grunt" active: bool = True offset: Vec3 = Vec3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0) mode: Mode = Mode.PATROL falloff: Curve = Curve() target: 'Entity' = None _inspector_buttons = [("explode", "Explode")] def explode(self): self.health = 0 Annotation Inspector widget Stored as float Number field float int Integer field int bool Checkbox bool str Text field string Annotated[float, Range(min, max[, step])] Float slider, default step 0.01 float clamped to range Annotated[int, Range(min, max)] Integer slider, default step 1 int clamped to range Vec2 / Vec3 / Vec4 Vector fields float components Enum subclass Dropdown of member names enum value 'Entity' Entity picker UUID; the live object is passed to the script Curve Curve editor keyframe set Details: Range is Range(min_value=0.0, max_value=1.0, step=None) . A plain [min, max] or (min, max[, step]) sequence in Annotated metadata works identically. Entity picker stores the target UUID in the scene and resolves the live object before each call — safe across renames, unlike name-based lookup. docs.text: Lifecycle Callbacks Every callback is optional. Define only what the behavior needs; the engine caches per-method lookups and skips missing ones without cost. Method Short alias Signature When it runs on_awake awake () Once when Play starts, before on_start ; use for caches and peer lookups on_start start () Once when Play starts; use for initial state and first actions on_update update (dt) Every rendered frame in scene order; dt already scaled by time scale on_fixed_update fixed_update (dt) Every physics step with stable dt ( 0.02 default); forces and movement here on_enable enable () When the entity becomes active ( entity.active = True ) on_disable disable () When the entity becomes inactive; stop loops and sounds here on_collision_enter — (other_id) or (other_id, force) Contact starts on_collision_stay — (other_id) or (other_id, force) Contact continues on_collision_exit — (other_id) or (other_id, force) Contact ends on_destroy destroy () Component removed or scene unloaded; release resources here gizmo_lines — () -> list Editor gizmo lines, runs outside Play too gizmo_meshes — () -> list Editor gizmo meshes, runs outside Play too Call order at Play start: on_awake for every scripted component, then on_start for every scripted component. Do not assume sibling start order — fetch peers lazily or in on_update guards. dt semantics: render dt stretches with slow motion and pause (time scale 0 freezes updates); fixed dt stays constant so physics and its scripts stay deterministic. Collision dispatch: the solver reports contacts to the physics layer, which maps solver bodies to entity ids and invokes callbacks. Arity is measured once from the signature — two parameters receive (other_id: str, force: float) , one parameter receives just other_id . Resolve the other entity inside the callback only if needed; id comparison is cheaper. Enable/disable: toggling entity.active fires on_disable / on_enable on all components of that entity, scripts included. Disabling mid-Play pauses that behavior without destroying its instance state. Destroy cases: removing the ScriptComponent in the editor, deleting the entity, unloading the scene, or stopping Play. Hot-reload recreates the instance but preserves Inspector field values and re-runs on_awake / on_start . Exceptions: any error in any callback is caught and logged as Script ... error ... with a traceback naming the script and method. The frame, the physics step and the remaining components continue. class Fighter: health: int = 100 def on_awake(self): self.hits = 0 self.body = self._entity.get_component_by_name("Rigidbody") def on_start(self): self.alive = True def on_update(self, dt): if self.health <= 0 and self.alive: self.alive = False self._entity.active = False def on_fixed_update(self, dt): if self.body and self.health <= 0: self.body.velocity = Vec3(0.0, 0.0, 0.0) def on_collision_enter(self, other_id, force): self.hits = self.hits + 1 self.health = self.health - int(force) def on_destroy(self): self.hits = 0 self.body = None

docs.text: Scripting Overview Entity behaviors in ZarinEngine are plain .py files with a behavior class. No base class, no registration boilerplate, no build step — the file itself is the asset. End-to-end flow: Project → Create → Python Script creates the file inside the project folder. Keep scripts next to the content that uses them; sibling imports (including Cython modules) resolve from the script folder automatically. Select an entity, Inspector → Add Component → Scripts , pick the file in the Script field. Annotated class attributes instantly become Inspector widgets. Tune values in the Inspector — they are stored in the scene ( .zpes ), not in the .py file, so one script drives many tuned instances. Press Play . The engine loads the class, instantiates it with no arguments, assigns self._entity , and calls on_awake then on_start . How it works inside: The engine finds the first class in alphabetical attribute order ( dir() order, not definition order) that declares at least one lifecycle callback, collision callback, gizmo method, or _inspector_buttons . Inheritance is not required; the constructor must take no arguments. Short names are full aliases: update = on_update , start = on_start , and so on for awake, fixed_update, destroy, enable, disable. If both variants are defined, the on_* version wins. One entity can hold several ScriptComponent instances ( _allow_multiple = True ): movement, health and visuals as separate scripts on one object. An exception inside any callback never crashes the game: it is written to the console with the script and method name, and the frame continues with the next component. script_path is stored relative to the project root, so scenes and scripts move between machines cleanly. Execution context: on_update(dt) runs in scene order every rendered frame with dt already multiplied by the time scale; on_fixed_update(dt) runs on the physics clock with a stable step ( 0.02 default). Collision callbacks arrive from the physics dispatch, not the ECS loop, with the other entity id and optionally the impact force. Gizmo methods ( gizmo_lines , gizmo_meshes ) execute in the editor even outside Play for custom handles and debug drawing. Performance guidance: scripts are Python and run per frame — keep on_update lean, cache component lookups in on_start instead of fetching by name every frame, and move number-crunching into Cython modules (see Cython in Scripts). Subpages: Lifecycle Callbacks — every method, signature and call order. Inspector Fields and Range — annotations to widgets, Entity pickers, buttons. Input and Math API — injected names, keys, axes, vectors, curves. Hot Reload — editing scripts during Play. Cython in Scripts — compiled helpers with zero manual builds. ScriptComponent — paths, flags, class resolution, Check. Script Examples — copy-paste behaviors.

docs.text: ScriptComponent ScriptComponent is the engine side of user scripts: it loads the .py file, builds Inspector fields from the class, forwards lifecycle calls, stores field values in the scene, and validates on demand. Component facts: script_path is stored relative to the project root, so scenes are portable. A relative path that does not resolve directly is retried against the project root; absolute paths resolve as-is. hot_reload defaults to True . Several ScriptComponent instances may live on one entity ( _allow_multiple = True ). The Inspector header shows the file display name (base name without extension) with a reveal action and an editor button; a second header lists the discovered script variables. Class resolution, in order: Modification-time short-circuit: unchanged mtime reuses the cached class with zero work. Import preparation: the script folder joins the module search so sibling .py and compiled Cython modules resolve. Error collection: syntax parse, core.* import checks, trial execution. On errors one consolidated Script '...' has N error(s): message is logged per file version, the old instance is dropped, and no fields render until the file is fixed. Module execution with the injected API ( Input , KeyCode , Vec2/3/4 , Curve , Range , Logger ). Class pick: the first class in alphabetical attribute order ( dir() order, not definition order) that declares at least one lifecycle callback, collision callback, gizmo method, or _inspector_buttons . Instantiated with no arguments; self._entity is assigned before every call. Method caching: bound methods per canonical name with fast flags for on_update / on_fixed_update ; collision arities measured once via signature inspection; field hints cached until the file changes. Serialization: script_path and the script_fields dict persist in .zpes , so tuned instances survive reloads, prefabs and version control. hot_reload (default True ) is a runtime-only flag and is not serialized. The Check action runs step 3 on demand and reports file:line: message rows — including the core.maths.math3d vs core.math3d hint and circular-import failures — so broken scripts are diagnosed without pressing Play. Multiple instances on one entity each keep an independent module state, instance and field set; they reload independently. Cross-script communication goes through the entity ( get_component by sibling script is resolved via its component, or shared state on the entity).

docs.text: Honest Scripting Limitations What the engine does not give you — each item verified against the source, with the supported alternative. 1. No Vec3.rotate Vec3 ( core/pyx/_math_vec.pyx ) exposes dot , cross , length , length_sq , normalized , to_list , zero , one , up , forward , right — there is no rotate method. Rotating a free vector is Quat.rotate_vec3(v) (same file). Rotating an object is Transform.rotate(euler: Vec3) taking euler degrees ( core/components/transform/tr/matrix.py:355 ). t.rotate(Vec3(0.0, 90.0 * dt, 0.0)) # yaw 90 deg/sec, NOT t.rotate(vector) 2. _call_py logs errors without a traceback core/components/scripting/scriptc/hotreload.py:253-260 : def _call_py(self, canonical, *args): ... try: meth(*args) except Exception as e: Logger.error(f"Script {canonical} error '{self.script_path}': {e}") Only str(e) is logged — no traceback, no line number. When a callback silently stops working, wrap suspect blocks yourself and log with traceback.format_exc() , or reproduce the logic outside Play mode. 3. Named axes return 0.0 until you DefineAxis Input.GetAxis(name) ( core/input/inpsys/gamepad.py ) returns 0.0 for any name missing from cls._state._axes — and mouse axes only after DefineMouseAxis . There are no pre-registered Horizontal / Vertical axes: call Input.DefineAxis("Horizontal", positive=[...], negative=[...], ...) (key codes from KeyCode ) before first use, once (e.g. in on_awake ). def on_awake(self): Input.DefineAxis("Horizontal", [KeyCode.D], [KeyCode.A]) Input.DefineAxis("Vertical", [KeyCode.W], [KeyCode.S]) def on_update(self, dt): x = Input.GetAxis("Horizontal") # 0.0 unless defined above 4. AudioSource.on_enable auto-starts playback core/components/audio/source/component.py:82-84 : def on_enable(self): if self.clip_path and not self._playing: self.play() Any disable→enable toggle restarts the clip (in addition to play_on_awake in on_start ). on_disable / on_destroy stop the voice. Workaround: keep clip_path empty until you explicitly play() , or gate enables behind your own flag. 5. A neighbouring .pyx triggers a blocking build Hot-reload watches Cython neighbours ( ext_sources_changed , unload_ext_modules in hotreload.py ); a stale .pyx is rebuilt synchronously by ensure_extensions(plugin_dir, background=False) with a per-file timeout ( core/foundation/plugin_cython.py ), and loaded via import_extension(package, module, fallback_dir) from the adjacent .pyd / .so . Keep script-side .pyx files small, or ship the prebuilt extension so frames never stall on a compile. 6. Threads: never touch Qt / GL / scene objects from workers Docks are QTimer -driven widgets and the viewport renders GL on the main Qt thread ( vr_dock.py , physviz/plugin.py , plotter_plugin/panel.py ). The codebase's own crossing pattern is a QueuedConnection dispatcher — plugins/zarin_mcp/main_thread.py : def run_on_main_thread(fn, timeout_ms=60000): ... Compute on worker threads, then marshal all engine/scene/Qt calls through main-thread dispatch. There is no thread-safe scene API. Verified against core/pyx/_math_vec.pyx , core/components/transform/tr/matrix.py , core/components/scripting/scriptc/hotreload.py , core/input/inpsys/gamepad.py , core/components/audio/source/component.py , core/foundation/plugin_cython.py , plugins/zarin_mcp/main_thread.py .
